precepts.label: Leviticus 11:44
precepts.why:
Many of our people who believe Christ is black and believe they are Israelites still struggle with Paul’s words: “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving”. They take it to mean, just pray over it and eat whatever you want. But what makes every creature good? “And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good for its purpose. Worms are one of the best ways to prepare land for planting, but we do not eat worms. Pigs were the garbage disposal, because they eat everything. Can you pray over a human foot and eat it?

The bottom feeders have a purpose too. Catfish, loaches, shrimp and snails are sold as natural tank cleaners: they eat the uneaten food, the algae and the waste. Put crab or any bottom feeder in murky water and in a few hours it will be clear. The filter you change in a fish tank is what you eat when you eat shrimp; that is why they are called the roaches of the sea. Lobster was once fed to prisoners. And pork carries the trichinella worm, which can travel into the muscles and even the brain. If a creature’s job is to eat garbage, what will it do to you? Gout, high cholesterol, hypertension, even lost fingers and feet.

Read the verse before and the verse after. The meats are “received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth”, and “thy law is the truth.” To believe is to keep the law: “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment; and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” And the creature “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Christians never read that far.

So where does the word of God sanctify the animals? Here: “ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He says it twice: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” And how are we holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.”

“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” You move like a flash when something comes at your eye; flee from sin that fast. John says, “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food, and overeating, is destroying the temple the Most High gave you to do his work. He wants a fit army: you cannot teach discipline in the street without having it yourself, and you cannot go to camp and become a liability.

precepts.label: Genesis 2:7
precepts.why:
“Let us make man in our image, after our likeness” is not talking about all people. The man is Adam, and verse 28 shows it: God blessed them and told them to “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” That is Adam and the line coming from him, which would eventually be the twelve tribes of Israel.

Genesis 2:7 is read together with it: “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” Formed from the dust of the ground: we know God is black, Christ is black and the apostles were black. The real Jews are black, and the Caucasian race, Esau as the Bible calls them, is cursed.

Solomon says the same in Wisdom of Solomon 7, that he is “the offspring of him that was first made of the earth”, and that God gave him to know “the operation of the elements.” The elements in the soil are the elements in man: oxygen, iron, calcium, sodium, potassium, magnesium, in different percentages. When God made us from the dust, he took from those elements and worked them to form man, the way he formed land and sea. That is what we call the periodic table today, and it is what Esau tries to do with his so-called science: play Frankenstein and try to become God.

But the image goes deeper than the dust and the skin. The breath God breathed in is wisdom, “the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” He gave it to us so that we would know better. Being made after his image and likeness is his spirit, the commandments of God.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:24
precepts.why:
After his image and after his likeness means his spirit, the commandments of God. A lot of the time people think the image and likeness only means looking like God. Ephesians 4:24 shows what his image is: “put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.”

That is after the image of God: created in righteousness. The man God made in his image was made to be righteous and holy, not only to share his color.

So being after his image is more than the hue of your skin. Black and wicked is not the way to go; you are still the devil. We say the white man is a devil, but there are black devils too. Just because you are black does not make you special unless you are righteous. It is the laws of God that make us special.

precepts.label: Psalms 17:15
precepts.why:
Genesis says “after our likeness”, and Psalms 17:15 shows what that likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is righteousness. David beholds God's face in righteousness and is satisfied to wake in his likeness. So man made after God's image and likeness was meant to be righteous.

Read with Ephesians 4:24, the new man “created in righteousness and true holiness”, it is plain: black is black, but being made in his image means being black and righteous, because black and wicked ain't the way to go: you're still the devil. We say the white man's a devil, but there's black devils too. Just because you are black don't make you special unless you are righteous; it is the laws of God that make us special. The dust of the ground made the body; keeping the commandments is what makes us his likeness.

precepts.label: Numbers 14:27-34
precepts.why:
Exodus 13:8 says “And thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the Lord did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt.” This is done means the feast of unleavened bread. But what did the Lord do unto me? The Lord delivered everyone, but did everyone enter the promised land? No. Numbers 14 shows what he did.

“How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me?” When we came out of Egypt, our people were evil. You thought they were righteous? They were rebellious: a bunch of liars, fornicators, murmurers. The Lord said, “as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward”. Once you were twenty years old and up, the Lord said, all of you are going to die. Aaron died. Moses died too; not that Moses was evil, but the people provoked him to anger, so he did not see the promised land, though when he left his body he was going back to paradise.

“Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.” Joshua and Caleb were the only two adults the Lord allowed to make it in. According to the law, at twenty you are the age of a man and take responsibility for yourself, which is why twenty is the age to marry. Everybody twenty and up, their blood was on their own head.

“But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised.” The children wandered forty years and bore the whoredoms of the adults, seeing all the evil they did, “until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness”: until every last one of those wicked Israelites died, everybody who had leaven in them, the murmurers, the adulterers, the ones who held on to Egypt.

So the me of Exodus 13:8 is not Moses. It is the little ones, twenty years and under, who grew up in the land and told their sons: we keep unleavened bread because the Lord purged the leaven out of me in the wilderness. And it is the same in the future: whoever keeps leaven, which is sin, through the seven days, that soul shall be cut off.

precepts.label: Exodus 20:5
precepts.why:
Exodus 34:7 says the Lord will “by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.” Exodus 20:5 shows who that is spoken of: “Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me.”

Of them that hate me. To disobey God's commandments is to demonstrate that you hate God. He pardons iniquity and transgression and sin, but if we are guilty of breaking his laws, we are going to pay.

That is why this is read in the wilderness, right after the commandments and statutes were given. A lot of us did not learn from the mistakes we made back then. We came back and did the same damn thing, still wicked and evil and covetous to this day, and the Most High is going to keep sending those afflictions until the lesson is learned. Read the book of your fathers to find out what we did and why all this hell is on us, and you will know what not to do today.

precepts.label: Exodus 20:17
precepts.why:
The iniquity visited upon the children in Exodus 34:7 is the same sin carried from generation to generation, and covetousness is one of them. “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.”

To covet means to take what does not belong to you: to take it by wickedness, by deceit. The same BS we were doing back then, we still do today, coveting our neighbour's house and our neighbour's wife.

Then, “nor his ox”: hold it right there. That points to Exodus 22, the same chapter Negroes use to beguile you sisters. The whole of that chapter is about thou shalt not covet. Then, “nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s”: you are not supposed to covet, to take, anything that belongs to that father, that neighbour.

So the iniquity of the fathers that is still being visited on us is the same covetousness, and we should learn not to carry that evil all the way up to now.

precepts.label: Exodus 22:1-17
precepts.why:
Exodus 22 is the law put in place for those that wanted to do evil, and it is proper. The whole chapter is about putting restraints on covetousness. It is not telling you how you are supposed to move. It is like a speeding ticket: your insurance goes way up, and that is the consequence of breaking the original law. Drive the damn speed limit.

“If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.” That is covetousness: you coveted thy neighbour's ox, exactly what Exodus 20:17 forbids. If you do, you pay for the one you stole and give him five oxen for it.

“And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.” The maid belongs to her father. To entice her means you coveted to get her; you did it behind the father's back, in deceit. You broke the tenth commandment, “nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.” You lured her away from her father, and you are going to try to tell me that is righteous? You are a damn fool. And a woman that has no wisdom will follow that and pay for the judgment.

Verse 17 kills it: “If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.” The father said hell no. Even though you enticed her, you are not taking her. That is what happened with Dinah: she was enticed, spoken to sweetly and kindly; she was not raped. Even though he wanted to marry her, her brothers said no, snatched her out of that house, and she had to sit there defiled.

That should be a warning to you women. No backdoor marriages will be approved, period. If we have to snatch you out, and you have to sit with that scarlet letter knowing you were defiled, that is better than being tied up with somebody that means you pure evil. How could you even respect a man who went behind your father's back, your protection's back? This is the guilty that Exodus 34:7 says the Lord will by no means clear.

It speaks mainly of the northern kingdom, but all of us are doing this now.

No truth: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” Truth is the Bible, the laws. Nobody in the land is adhering to “Do not prostitute thy daughter”; nobody is paying attention to it or bringing that precaution into the land. No mercy: people get killed over this. Brothers have gone to jail and been shot down over it. No knowledge of God, meaning his commandments: the priest's lips should keep knowledge and the people should seek the law at his mouth, and they are not getting it at all.

“By swearing, and lying”. We heard complete lies two weeks ago: a man told everybody that nobody had told him to leave the sister alone, to make it look as if the leadership didn't know what was going on. Brothers had to stand up, bring him right back to his lying statement, and correct his wicked ass in front of everybody, so nobody would think he had a toe to stand on to justify the evil he did. Then: “and killing, and stealing”: we saw that in the videos.

All of it because the woman was taught to let her behind hang out. The Bible gives a dress code: cover your ass. The Lord gave a dress code because he knows that when the clothes come off, all kinds of things go on. David saw Bathsheba, and he lost it all. Then: “and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood”. People get stabbed and shot up, all because she had her clothes off in the street. Do you see the connection?

So “full of wickedness” means literally full of wickedness: that is what you get when God's laws are not taught, no Bible, no scruples, no laws. Having kids through backdoor marriages produces madness like this. That is done here. You're going to do it right or you ain't going to do it at all; nobody is holding a ceremony over fornication. It starts with the fathers and mothers, who must not prostitute the daughter, because the enemy goes after the women: mess them up and the children are done.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 4:13
precepts.why:
Who was the Lord talking to in 2 Chronicles 7? Solomon. “if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked”, and “if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes”, then “will I pluck them up by the roots”. So what was Solomon's problem, outside of the sin itself? Solomon tells it on himself: “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.”

That was his problem. He couldn't take correction. He didn't want to hear it; nobody could tell him nothing. That's like some brothers here: they can't be told, they don't want to hear it, they get offended. He was an old, foolish king who could no longer be admonished, and from that trickled all the other problems he had.

Even Solomon at the end understood the whole duty of man: to fear God and keep his commandments. But he shouldn't have had to go through that. All wisdom was given to him, and he saw his father's life before his eyes. He was concerned with how the world operated and wanted to experience the world, when we are supposed to be unspotted from this world.

So the forsaking that brought the captivity began with a king who could not be admonished. When you keep repeating something to people who can't be told anything, after a while you lose them. That is why we have to be willing to receive correction.

precepts.label: Proverbs 15:10
precepts.why:
The Lord warned Solomon, “if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes and my commandments”; to forsake means to abandon, desert or leave something entirely, a breach of duty, to totally turn your back. Proverbs ties forsaking to hating correction: “Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die.”

When you have forsaken the way, being corrected is grievous to you. You keep having to be told the same thing over and over, and the one who doesn't want to hear it gets pissed off; he doesn't want to hear it no more. That was Solomon, the old and foolish king who would no more be admonished.

And the end of it is death: “he that hateth reproof shall die.” For Israel it meant being plucked up by the roots out of the land and made a proverb and a byword among all nations. Reading that is understanding why we are in captivity today. We got jammed up because we would not take correction.

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:1
precepts.why:
“He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.” Often reproved means every time the correction comes, he will not accept it. So he gets corrected over and over, and after a while his neck becomes hardened. He becomes stiffnecked. The scriptures don't have that effect on him anymore; there is no contriteness, no shame. You see brothers always getting stood up, and after a while it's, yeah, okay, put me out, I'll be back.

Why does that happen? The word of God is not moving you to change. You can't be the same person you were before; there has to be some type of growth. How do you find yourself doing the same thing you were doing ten years ago? Why, ten years later, does somebody have to motivate you to go do the work? Something is not firing off; something is disconnected.

The word of God is supposed to inspire you to change. The word of God changes you; the word of God can cure you. If you ain't changing, it is one of two things: you are a heathen, or you are a reprobate, and the kingdom ain't for you. So if it is not working, examine whether you even believe.

That is the other side of 2 Chronicles 7:14. The Lord will hear and forgive and heal the land when his people humble themselves and turn from their wicked ways. The one who hardens his neck against reproof is suddenly destroyed, and that without remedy.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 19:13-15
precepts.why:
The wicked of Psalms 50 hates instruction and casts God's words behind him, and “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Sirach shows the right way to deal with a brother or friend: “Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.”

“Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.”

So why do we sit and speak against our brother? Because sometimes a brother admonishes you, and now you are angry behind it. Why are you mad? Why is it bothering you? Admonishing is what a friend is supposed to do. The one who hates instruction turns the admonishment around and slanders the brother who gave it.

God says to that man, “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee”. Just because he didn't do anything right away, don't think you are going to get away with it.

precepts.label: Proverbs 18:24
precepts.why:
Why is a friend's admonishment the same matter as speaking against your brother? Because friend and brother are synonymous. Proverbs explains it: “A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.”

There are some friends that are closer than a brother. So when Psalms 50:20 says “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son”, the slander lands on the friend who admonished you as much as on your own blood.

A man that has friends must show himself friendly, not turn on the friend who corrects him. And God will not keep silence forever: “Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.” That is Israel, because the other nations never knew God to forget him. “and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God”, and the salvation is only to Israel.

precepts.label: Romans 6:1
precepts.why:
The question put to the class: you're alone online late at night, temptation hits, and nobody from the congregation would know. What shows integrity? A, entertain the temptation privately. B, watch a little and justify it later. C, cut it off immediately and fight temptation. D, convince yourself grace covers everything. Answer D is a scary mindset to have, and Paul already answered it: “What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?”

Shall we continue in sin that grace may cover everything? That is a terrible mindset, and it is the mindset of Christianity: I found grace, grace covers me, I can do what I want when I want. All I have to do is believe in Jesus; I ain't got to do nothing he says, just believe he's my Lord and savior. Christianity is evil.

The answer is C. The questions are easy and the answers are easy; the problem is when it comes to fruition in real time. You are fighting your war against yourself: you don't want to push play, but you want to push play, and nobody is there to tell you a damn thing. That is when C gets blurred out.

The real battlefield is private. A lot of people fall spiritually in secret long before they fall publicly. The representative shows up at the Sabbath; the real you shows up at home, alone, with your family, and your wife knows exactly who you are. You can't salute so hard you're over righteous and then go home and verbally, financially or physically abuse your wife. And sisters, you can't bow 90 degrees at the door and then go home, cuss your husband out, and keep a filthy house. That is lacking integrity and poor character.

That is Proverbs 11:3: “The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.” Grace is not a cover for sin; integrity is acting on what you know, even when nobody is watching.

precepts.label: Titus 1:13
precepts.why:
“A true witness delivereth souls”: a true prophet, a true servant, delivers souls. Paul shows how a true witness does it: “This witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith.”

It is our job, brothers, to rebuke our people sharply. Why? That they may be sound in the faith; that they may repent. That is how souls are delivered.

So whose soul have you been delivering? You have been sitting here five years, seven years, ten years; some of you cannot even deliver your own soul, because you forgot the mission. Who are you working for, spiritually: Messiah or Satan? Some of you are agents working for Esau.

“but a deceitful witness speaketh lies.” Our people love lies, and the deceitful witness feeds them lies. That is why you see ten thousand, twenty thousand in the Christian churches: they do not want the truth. They say Christ cannot be black, Christ cannot come only for the Israelite. The truth to us is a foreign language. That is why the true witness has to rebuke sharply: sharp rebuke is what brings a people who love lies to repentance.

precepts.label: Romans 8:29
precepts.why:
“In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence.” Some of you have no confidence and low self-esteem because you have no fear of God, sitting in the same seat for seven years. Romans shows what God called you for: “For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

What does it mean to be conformed? To change. We must change to the image of Jesus Christ. Some of you have not changed yet, and we can see it.

We can see the potential on you: this brother has the spirit to do great things in Israel. But you have to see it. My job as a deacon is to push your spirit and to build you up, but no matter how much I build you up, if you cannot see it, I cannot make you see it. You have to get up and see it yourself.

There is a lot of work to do while you are waiting for the kingdom, and the kingdom does not come by observation. When temptation and tribulation come, the one who has not been conformed will run, because mentally and spiritually he is not strong enough to endure it. Being predestinated to be conformed means you have to do the changing.

precepts.label: Ephesians 1:5
precepts.why:
“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.” The same God who foreknew us and predestinated us to be conformed to the image of his Son predestinated us unto the adoption of children, by Jesus Christ, to himself.

That calling is what the class carried straight into Paul: “For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of: for necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!” Paul understood he was a servant, sent to serve the people and deliver souls. Destruction unto me if I do not do what I was sent to do.

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward.” You have to do it willingly, not because somebody forced you; a brother forced to do something has no spirit in it. Yet some of you get up at four in the morning and willingly give the white man eight or twelve hours without complaining, while coming here on the Sabbath is a burden.

So being predestinated as children by Jesus Christ is not a reason to sit and wait. God did not call you here just to sit and listen. It is a call to be the true witness that delivers souls, and in the fear of the Lord is the strong confidence to do it.

precepts.label: Proverbs 17:10
precepts.why:
“He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul”. He doesn't want to hear it; he doesn't want to be corrected; he's always right, but wrong as hell. That isn't hurting somebody else; you are destroying your own soul, because you can't be corrected, which means you can't grow. This is why: “A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool.”

As a foolish person, you cannot allow wisdom to enter in. You're sitting around the men, you're in the school with all these men, you see everybody growing around you, and for some reason you know everything, but the wisdom can't take hold and exalt you the way it exalts all the rest who take hold of it. You're fighting against it.

That is why some have been in the truth 10 or 15 years and are still a soldier. How long you been with us? 10 years. What's your rank? Officer of 10, sir. Why? I don't know, sir. You know. You know everything else but that. You can't say you've been held back. Ten years and you're only able to deal with ten men: that is a problem.

That is when it is time to take stock in yourself, and a lot of people don't want to do that, because they don't want the integrity that comes with the Bible. The one who hears reproof gets understanding; the fool takes a hundred stripes and learns nothing.

thread.label: Proverbs 16:6
thread.text: By mercy and truth iniquity is purged: and by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil.

classes.title: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.label: John 15:1-5
precepts.why:
“By mercy and truth iniquity is purged.” Going into Passover season, which is also purging season, we refocus and get rid of the spiritual leaven known as sin. Christ shows how the purging is done: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.”

A vine is nothing more than a root sprouting through the ground, and Christ is that root: “I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.” And the Father is the husbandman because we are what he planted: “ye are God’s husbandry, ye are God’s building.” We are his plants, his trees, which in that day become the trees of righteousness.

“Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away.” That is why we cannot be like the brother who had the talent and hid it. If we do not bring forth fruit, he takes away our candlestick: you did not do what I created you to do, so you cannot be here. One bad apple spoils the bunch, and you are going to hinder growth, so you have to be taken out of the way.

“and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” That is the purging of Proverbs 16:6: iniquity purged, so we keep growing in the spirit and getting closer to our Lord and our God.

“Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.” We have to stay steadfast and abide in Christ: not loving our pleasures or our lust more than Christ, but doing the will of the Father and his Son.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:19-21
precepts.why:
“Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his.” The Lord already knows who are his; we do not, but God does. And God also establishes leaders to guide you along the way, so that you do not fall into the wiles of Satan or stumble into pitfalls and never recover.

“And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” That is purging from sin, from the spiritual leaven, the same as “by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil.”

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is Israel. Just as not all the crops take root, in the house of Israel you have the good ones and the bad ones, some to honour and some to dishonour.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these”: not from the gold and silver, but from the wood and the earth. Those who are not producing fruit, those with dead spirits, those always caught up in some mess, those who separate from the leaders the Lord established. How did you learn what the new moon was? You saw a video of our leadership teaching it. But then you come in here and do not want to be around them; you want to be with the clique in the back. That is the wood and the earth, and God is telling you to purge yourself from those people if you want to remain steadfast in Christ.

Then “he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” God can use you.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 1:4-9
precepts.why:
“Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.” That escape from corruption is the purging of iniquity in Proverbs 16:6, and it has to be kept up.

“And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue.” We have to be diligent. We cannot just come in here knowing that Christ is black, God is black and the angels are black. When we come through these doors we have to add to our repertoire, add to our spirit: “virtue; and to virtue knowledge; And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity.”

“For if these things be in you, and abound”: not just be in you, but be in you and grow. “they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Meaning you do not have to be purged out. If you can do that, you do not have to worry about being taken out of the mix, because you are constantly growing and doing the Lord’s will.

“But he that lacketh these things is blind.” Sin has blinded you. You cannot think straight, you cannot do what is common sense, you struggle constantly and never break through, because you have not purged yourself from the wrong people and you love that pleasure more than God. He “cannot see afar off”: you cannot see that America is going to be destroyed and that salvation is coming. You are a situational Israelite living in the moment, thinking America is going to last forever. Shame.

He “hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.” God purged you from your old sins, but if you do not keep trimming, if you do not keep purging, you will end up back in your old folly. This is a wake-up call, a punch in the gut: come up out of the foolishness.

classes.title: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.label: Sirach 7:36
precepts.why:
“Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.” A hasty man acts off of impulse, and the answer to that is not to act off of impulse but to think it through: “Whatsoever thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt never do amiss.”

Whatever we take in hand, we remember the end. We have to be in that frame of mind, and we have to be around the right people, being around the righteous and staying occupied in the work. Whoever commits sin while being around the righteous family, Satan is heavy on him.

So when we are tempted, we can think things through and remember the judgment of the Lord, and the fear activates, and then we can overcome.

That is the whole choice set out in Romans 6: “Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” Fall into sin and in that moment you are serving the devil, because you cannot have two masters. Remembering the end is how a hasty man learns patience, resolve and discipline.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:15
precepts.why:
“Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God.” We have to be diligent, constantly abounding in the work, because if we are not, we can fall from the grace of God.

“lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you.” If you are not occupied in doing the Lord’s work, not putting your hands to the plow, not studying, not being amongst the righteous, a root of bitterness can spring up in you, because you are not studying to combat it. You might have a feeling, but you had better rebuke that thing, and the way to do it is to be around these people.

If you draw back and separate from your people, Satan has you right where he wants you. Now he can play on your psyche and your mind. When you are not constantly seeing people you start thinking differently: they never liked you anyway. That is what Satan does.

“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.” Satan wants to devour all of us, just as Christ told Peter that Satan desired to have him to sift him as wheat. We have to be in that mindset and know what is going on. The hasty man who does not look diligently lets bitterness spring up, and he is worse off than a fool.

precepts.label: Sirach 32:17
precepts.why:
“A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” When you hear a class like this, do not say, Oh, that ain’t it. You are just making an excuse to go back to your pleasure and your lust, to feel comfortable in them.

The excuse maker starts a fight over the chicken so he can leave and get some duck. It is like the story the Bishop told about the co-worker who dealt with multiple women and would start a fight with one to go see the other. Now you are pointing the finger at everybody else, when back at the ranch you really want to go have fun in your pleasure and your lust. As the Bishop’s graphic says, a sin-filled soul will find and make excuses only to fulfill its lust. That is very dangerous.

“A wicked soul shall destroy him that hath it, and shall make him to be laughed to scorn of his enemies.” And “Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.”

So we have to have fear and we have to be diligent if we want a fighting chance. The man hasty in his words, who always has an excuse ready, will not be reproved, and that is why there is more hope of a fool than of him.

precepts.label: Sirach 23:2
precepts.why:
The hasty man needs control, and control comes by discipline: “Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins.” We have to learn discipline so we do not end up looking crazy out here.

“For the very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline; and the care of discipline is love.” The very true beginning of following after wisdom is the desire of discipline. So we have to fight temptation, fight off the devil and overcome the beast in order to learn that discipline.

“Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.” We have to put on all of the armour. If you are not studying, you are not battling; you are just falling victim.

Keeping God’s commandments does not give instant gratification. The consequences are delayed: we are going to get the kingdom. Sin gives you the pleasure right then and there, the instant dopamine, and once you are hardened by the deceitfulness of sin you no longer see any reason to keep God’s commandments because they do nothing for you in the moment. In this truth you have to self-motivate. You cannot wait for somebody else to give you a pep talk. You have to discipline your own soul if you want to make it.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 16:50
precepts.why:
“So shall righteousness hate iniquity, when she decketh herself, and shall accuse her to her face, when he cometh that shall defend him that diligently searcheth out every sin upon earth.” We have to learn to hate iniquity. We have to discipline our minds to hate iniquity and to hate sin. If we want the Lord to defend us, that is what we have to do.

Wisdom of Solomon shows the end of both sides. The ungodly say, “Even so we in like manner, as soon as we were born, began to draw to our end, and had no sign of virtue to shew; but were consumed in our own wickedness.” The hope of the ungodly “is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.”

“But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.” You may not see it right now, but if you keep God’s commandments, if you do the homework, you are going to live forever, while everything that feels good in the moment passes away. The Most High cares for you, if you are able to hate sin.

That is the answer to the hasty man: discipline the mind to hate iniquity, and the Lord defends the one who diligently searches out every sin.

thread.label: Ecclesiastes 7:26
thread.text: And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.

classes.title: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.label: Sirach 25:26
precepts.why:
“whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.” A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man. But what about the man who complains of a wicked woman and claims he is not wicked himself? If that is true, he will find a way to escape. Sirach shows the way: “If she go not as thou wouldest have her, cut her off from thy flesh, and give her a bill of divorce, and let her go.”

This is the brother in the world trying to repent, trying to get his house in order and straighten it out, while his wife keeps up the traps of Ecclesiastes 7:26: her heart snares and nets, her hands as bands, creating chaos and assignments so he can't get to camp, to the brothers, to the meetings. She doesn't want to listen. Then let her go. And it goes both ways; it is about you men too.

But understand: this is not talking about a biblical marriage. Once you get married in this truth, she is yours for life, unless she commits adultery. There is no divorce in the Bible, and we don't dissolve marriages up in here; it is written in our rules. This is for those coming in from outside this truth, with all kinds of situations.

So the man who pleases God escapes from her. But if you allow yourself to be destroyed, you were indeed wicked, and the woman sent to you was your portion for real.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 7:15
precepts.why:
Paul speaks to the same case: “But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases: but God hath called us to peace.”

The man was wicked and inherited a wicked woman. Why? God orchestrated it, to see whether he would stay there, and to reflect what is in us so that we can change. The Lord is interested in the elect, so he puts us through trials and temptations to see if we will overcome them.

The bondage is the worldly marriage. When the spouse says, I don't care what you do, I want nothing to do with that Bible, and makes it plain and won't bend, still cooking pork and ham hocks on one side of the stove, this half is for you since you're keeping those laws, we're going to keep eating chitlins and hog maws, the house smelling like butt: if the unbelieving depart, let them depart. That is the woman of Ecclesiastes 7:26 whose heart is traps and nets, and whoso pleases God shall escape.

But those coming out of these situations have a lot of work to do before they can even think about properly marrying, and brothers and sisters are impatient. Leadership are the fathers of the men and women, and we have the records. When we tell you to lean back and let the brother or sister work on themselves, it is for a good reason, because the backdoor marriage stories are horrible, and they get worse every time a new one pops up.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:1-4
precepts.why:
Before anyone walks away, look at the other side. At a Passover panel years ago a sister asked when she could walk away from her husband in the world. They had been together about ten years, through Africanism, through Islam, through different things. In his mind this truth might be just another fad. Wait, sister. Lean back.

“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.” He is worldly, but he isn't telling you to break the laws of God, so still deal with him properly. Chaste means with discipline: you aren't cursing him out. He watches the change in you, sees the fear of the Lord in you, and sees it is serious, not a phase.

“Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart”, “the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.” She puts on proper clothing, and tells him: my husband, I want you to come in and take command, so I can deal with you as a proper wife. He comes home from catching hell at work and she knows how to pull him out of it, and he asks, where are you learning this wisdom? If he is righteous, he comes in behind you; we have seen it many times.

Men do the same: a brother who was in sin with his wife last week wants to turn the house upside down this week. Give her a chance to see you're serious. Wives have said, I didn't know he was this serious; he was willing to let me go, and they came in behind him. That is the Most High giving righteousness to righteousness.

precepts.label: Revelation 5:12-13
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the wilderness and the desert shall be glad and “blossom as the rose.” When we are delivered, the desert places in our land will blossom and trees will start springing up, because we are connected to the earth. When the righteous people start ruling, everything changes. The animals are free, and the creatures understand us. That may sound like church talk, but the donkey did talk to Balaam: why are you beating me? Revelation shows how far that understanding goes.

“Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.” Christ receives all these things.

“And every creature which is in heaven”: those are the angels. There are creatures in heaven. “and on the earth”: the animals created on the earth. “and under the earth”: creatures created in the earth, worms and such, and creatures living deep in the earth that nobody has ever seen. “and such as are in the sea”: leviathan, and creatures in the sea no human being has ever seen, that the Lord created. “and all that are in them”: everything that was created.

“heard I saying, Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever.” They heard what John said, and they understood it, all the creatures.

That is why the land itself rejoices in Isaiah 35. The whole creation answers to the Lord, and when “the glory of Lebanon” is given and they “see the glory of the Lord, and the excellency of our God”, it is because the Lord will be on the earth, and everything will change.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 3:16
precepts.why:
God is “declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done.” Only the God of Israel can do that, and he shows the end to the prophets. Look at the videos of the missiles coming down at night: don't they look like stars falling from heaven? The prophets had never seen a missile, an Iron Dome, a supersonic missile or a nuclear weapon. They described what they saw to the best of their ability, and it is our job to put it together. Put yourself in the prophet's shoes, because you are the prophets; you just don't remember.

Habakkuk describes how it hurts when these missiles hit, because when they hit they bring destruction. You don't want to be around when a missile hits the ground; you don't even want to be ten feet away.

“When I heard, my belly trembled.” That kind of fear is an anxiety sitting inside you, in your chest. He cannot believe what he is watching, but the Lord had to show it to him. “My lips quivered at the voice”: he was shaking, he couldn't even talk straight. “Rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself.” He could not believe the damage this thing was doing, the number of people it killed when it hit.

“That I might rest in the day of trouble.” He is saying, I don't want to be alive to see this. It is so bad I don't want to be around to see it. That is what Psalms 91 means by a thousand falling at thy side and ten thousand at thy right hand: he saw the bomb drop and ten thousand people die right there.

That is the end God declared from the beginning, and “My counsel shall stand.” The media say Hamas is finished, Hezbollah has no weapons, Iran is weak; yet Hezbollah fired a hundred missiles into Israel the other day, and Israel cannot destroy Hamas under its nose while Iran is seven times bigger than Israel. precepts.label: Proverbs 22:6
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says the proverb will be used against us: “As is the mother, so is her daughter.” Very rarely do you see a fat mother and a skinny daughter. If the mama is big, the daughter is big, and if there is a son, he is really big too, because what you eat to get there is exactly what the kids have in the house to eat. The kid models himself or herself after the parents. If you are in the house working out, your kids will want to do push-ups and pull-ups and be in the gym with you. If you like to lie on the bed eating ice cream, they will lie in the bed eating ice cream with you. That self-hatred gets passed on, and that is how the cycle continues: grandmama's fat, mama's fat, the kid is fat, and they all give the same excuse, my thyroid, we big boned. Garbage.

So Proverbs gives the command: “Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” It is you that has to shape and mould the trajectory of the kid's life. That goes from teaching them the laws, to showing them what is good to eat and what is not good to eat, to showing them to exercise and to do their studies: train them in the right direction in every aspect.

If there is no candy in the house, can a six-year-old go outside and buy candy? Hell no. If there are no donuts in the house, can a six-year-old go and buy donuts? The kid eats what you feed them. And stop giving your kids choices: put sugary food and good food before a kid and ask what they want, and they will always choose sugar. A kid does not know. When your kid loves a healthy food, give it to them all the time.

If you are big and your kid is big, how will you feel when your young kid needs insulin shots because he is diabetic from being overfed on all kinds of garbage? Where is the love in that? Laziness is why a lot of the time we don't deal with our kids right and we don't deal with ourselves right. If we want to save our kids, it starts with you first: control your eating and exercise, and then you are setting the right example, so that the daughter who is as her mother is trained in the right way.

precepts.label: Hebrews 8:10-11
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant”. The rod is correction. And the bond of the covenant is the new covenant in Hebrews: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord”. After those days means after we are delivered out of here, out of this new Egypt, America.

“I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people”. Meaning we are going to know God's laws and we will keep God's laws. Right now it can be routine: you go to work every day, stop in the donut store for a donut and your coffee, eat the donut, and then remember, damn, it's the days of unleavened bread, how could I forget? But the Lord God says his laws will be in our minds. We are not going to forget, and we will do them and serve him. That is the new covenant. We are in the beginning of it now, but once Christ returns it will be fully established in the wilderness.

“And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.” All of us will know the Lord, from the least amongst us to the greatest. You won't have to go and teach anybody, because the Lord is going to teach us. Every custom and thought we learned in America has to go, and he will show us even the parts we are missing now, like the sun and the moon working together for the times and seasons, wisdom destroyed from amongst us through slavery.

So being brought into the bond of the covenant is us being purged in the wilderness again. As he pleaded with our fathers and got rid of the leaven from amongst them, he will “purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”: those that break God's laws, those with leaven in them. Many will be delivered out of here, but not everyone is going to make it into the promised land. Those who enter will have his laws written in their hearts.

precepts.label: Additions to Esther 13:18
precepts.why:
“in their affliction they will seek me early.” God returns to his place, and our people have to seek him, but they have to be afflicted first. That is how our people are. And the afflictions are just starting. We have been getting killed in the street by police, but that ain't it; that is only the prelude to what is about to happen.

Esau is turning back the hands of the civil rights era right now, and that is good, because black people trust in their oppression. Memphis, maybe the blackest city in America, has been gerrymandered and carved up and parcelled out to the outskirts of the state so no black man can win a congressional seat there anymore, and it is happening in Texas and everywhere. An elected black congressman was hauled out by state troopers, protesting that he was an elected official and lawfully there. White guilt is out the window. Our people swear they are going to vote their way out of this, and they need the affliction, to see the devil for who he is.

In Esther's day: “All Israel in like manner cried most earnestly unto the Lord, because their death was before their eyes.” That is when our people are going to come: when death is before their eyes, they will cry earnestly and look for God. Right now they are still confused about who the devil is.

The church that once organized the community and planned the votes is silent while the civil rights laws are turned back, while our people are found hanged in 2026 with their organs taken out and it is called suicide. The only ones crying out about it are the Israelites. So it is our job to warn our people and bring them to repentance, and when they come with death before their eyes, we will show them what they are doing wrong and how to get right.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 2:1-3
precepts.why:
Our people will cry earnestly when death is before their eyes, and Zephaniah says what to do before it comes: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.”

“Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” If you are seeking righteousness, you are admitting that you don't have it yet; you are walking in error and correcting it. So pray, Lord, show me where I am in error so I can fix it, so that when your decree brings forth I am lined up on the right side. That means when somebody is sent to tell you, this is wrong, you hear it and learn, because you don't want to be on the outside of what is about to happen.

So when you come to the house of learning and somebody shows you your error, don't get mad and leave. Leaving means going back out there to face the fierce anger of God unprepared. While you are here, you are going to learn how to turn away from your sins.

As we see these afflictions happening, we know the judgment and the fierce anger of the Lord are coming. Our people are clueless about what is about to happen to them; in America we are so comfortable that hard living means cancelling Netflix. It is our job to warn them, and they have to be willing to listen and be gathered before the decree brings forth.

precepts.label: Sirach 31:13
precepts.why:
“Remember that a wicked eye is an evil thing: and what is created more wicked than an eye? therefore it weepeth upon every occasion.” The eye is where it starts. It starts with the desire of what you see, and then the mind decides whether to feed the lust.

That is why it belongs with Matthew 15. The Pharisees were arguing about eating with unwashed hands, and Christ told them that what goes in at the mouth goes into the belly and “is cast out into the draught”, but “those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.” What comes out of your mouth is the output value of what was put into your mind, and the eye is one of the ways it gets put in.

The brain stores everything you let in. A random song or thought from years ago comes out of you because it was saved in long-term memory, the same way your stuff on the internet never really leaves. What you put into your vessel determines what comes out, and a lot of times we don't even realize we are being controlled. You were made in a factory called America, and those are not your words. The only way to break that code is to reprogram and recode, and the wicked eye is where the guarding has to begin.

precepts.label: Job 31:1
precepts.why:
“I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?” Job had to literally make a covenant: I'm not going to watch that, and if it gets within my eyesight, I got to turn away. I got to train my eyes to look away.

That is the three-second rule. The eyes are input. If you let yourself look at something for more than three seconds, it goes into your working memory, your short-term memory; keep looking at it and you are programming yourself into long-term memory. Turn away within three seconds and it doesn't have time to work within your memory. That is why TikTok gives you three seconds to capture somebody's attention, and why Netflix keeps it moving: once they have your attention through your eyes, they have you. Our eyes are the portal to take control over your vessel.

The algorithm is a reflection of you. Your searches and your scrolls tell who you are, what makes you sad, what makes you mad, what music you play when you're angry. So when you say the algorithm got you, it's not them getting you. It's you, manifested on a screen. The devil don't make you do anything you don't want to do.

David said the same: “I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes.” Train your eyes. If a show is full of action but something enticing comes on that goes against your values and your struggles, turn it off, click by. If you hear gossip or something negative, leave the conversation, because three seconds of listening will taint you, and three seconds of something negatively influencing you will control you.

Christ told the disciples he must go to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed and be raised again the third day. That was a good thing: he had to die to redeem the nation of Israel. But Peter took him and rebuked him: “Be it far from thee, Lord”. And Christ turned and said, “Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me”. What happened there? Satan literally jumped on Peter. That was not Peter; that was Satan talking to Christ through Peter, and Christ was talking to Satan.

Luke shows how that could be. After the temptation in the wilderness: “And when the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.” For a season. You think Satan stopped tempting Christ? He never stopped. He just left for a season and kept coming in different ways. When Christ was about to be crucified, Satan came back, and he came by jumping on Peter.

That is why Christ told Peter in another place that Satan desired to have him, to sift him as wheat, but that he had prayed for him that his faith fail not.

Satan comes for all of us; that is his job. For some it is money, for some it is sex, for some it is hatred. He comes at your weakness. So examine yourself: what is my weakness? That is what you need to strengthen, because that is what Satan will try to destroy you with. The worst are the ones who say they have no weakness; they deal with the heaviest demons and are just good at hiding it. The war is in your mind: when the evil thought comes, rebuke it, as Christ did: get thee behind me.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 5:6-7
precepts.why:
Christ likens the kingdom to leaven hid in three measures of meal “till the whole was leavened.” Leaven grows. Paul shows the other side of that same truth: “Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?” Because leaven grows, if you allow it to remain amongst other Israelites, that leaven is going to spread and defile others.

So the command is “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened.” We have to purge out the leaven within our own spirits and within our various congregations. God purged you from your old sins, but if you don't keep trimming, if you don't keep purging, you will end up back in your old folly.

“For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. Christ was sacrificed for us, so we no longer live unto ourselves; now we live unto Christ. This is a wake-up call, a readjustment, a punch in the gut: come up out of the foolishness and stop it.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:6-12
precepts.why:
“Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” Christ was warning the twelve of the leaven. Christ was the leader, and when leaders try to warn you of leaven, you need to listen. He knew what he was talking about.

The disciples “reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have taken no bread.” No, he was not talking about bread. He reminded them of “the five loaves of the five thousand” and “the seven loaves of the four thousand”: it's not about the bread, pay attention. They couldn't receive it at that time, until “Then understood they how that he bade them not beware of the leaven of bread, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” The leaven is their doctrine and their sinful nature. Don't get caught up in the things they do: they say and do not, they are hypocrites.

And the Pharisees and the Sadducees were Israelites. That doesn't mean we have anything against anybody, but when you see a spirit on someone who can influence you negatively, beware. It's up to you to listen, but the best thing is to follow, listen and consider the end of their conversation. Be very, very mindful.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 2:11
precepts.why:
“Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” Every year the Passover comes around and we see the same thing happen: people start bugging out. And people who have been with us, who saw it happen before, still fall for it. We have to fight. Don't play into Satan's devices.

He wants you right where he's got you. Some are on their way out because they're not paying attention to class, not studying, not praying, not getting their four chapters, not doing anything right. Satan has you right where he wants you.

We should not be ignorant of his devices, but some remain ignorant, and the reason is that they despise wisdom and don't want to be taught. That is how the leaven gets in and spreads.

precepts.label: Sirach 21:12
precepts.why:
Some don't want to be taught, and Sirach says why: “He that is not wise will not be taught”. If you're a fool, it doesn't matter what somebody does for you; you will not be taught, you will not retain it, it's not going to work for you.

“but there is a wisdom which multiplieth bitterness”. That wisdom is seeing it your own way, doing your own thing, and you're going to have a bitter end because of it.

Sirach 3:26 shows that bitterness: “A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last”. You're stubborn and don't want to learn; when wise words come out you're in the back, or you've got that hatred, something against somebody, so you don't want to hear nothing from them. And “he that loveth danger shall perish therein”. People like that are very dangerous; they can get people hurt if you follow after them. They perish in their folly, because they are unwise and not taught, because fools despise knowledge.

precepts.label: Sirach 10:12
precepts.why:
This tends to happen every year around the Passover, and this is a call to wake some up so they can get their mind right. “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God”. When you notice that your study habits have changed, when you notice that you're pulling back from the believers, understand that pride has now set in. You are regressing, going backwards.

“and his heart is turned away from his Maker”. That sin, that leaven, is now blinding you, so that you can no longer see clearly. That is the leaven spreading through the whole lump: it starts small, with a pulling back, and grows until the heart is turned away from the Most High.

precepts.label: Hebrews 3:13
precepts.why:
“But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day”. How often? Daily. Exhortation can't take place if you're not around nobody. The Bible is telling us what to do: stay around each other, stay around the righteous daily.

“lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin”. Sin may feel good, but it's a deceiver, because you think you can get that feeling constantly. You can't; it's temporal, only for a certain amount of time. If we pull away, sin can take over our mind and we may never recover. That's the scary part.

2 Thessalonians 2 shows it. “Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”: America came after the workings of Satan, making you think God is with them, and it's time to come up out of the beast and separate. “And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.” They loved their pleasures more than God, deceived by the pleasures of sin. “And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion”. You can be deceived by sin so bad you may never recover your soul: still alive, still living, but a dead soul and a dead spirit. Be very mindful.

The scripture says choose life, but if you do not know what the law says, how are you going to choose life?

Solomon shows the way to life: “My son, keep my words, and lay up my commandments with thee. Keep my commandments, and live”. If you are not keeping the laws, you are not going to live. So when you keep eating unclean food and are not controlling what you eat, you are sinning.

“And my law as the apple of thine eye.” If somebody tried to poke your eye, you would move fast, like flash, because you do not take chances with something that could blind you. If somebody poked your arm you would not move that fast. The same way you protect your eye, you should protect the law. The moment anything tries to make you go against God’s law, you should move fast. But too many are like a fly drawn to the light that is about to kill it: instead of moving away, they keep going toward it.

The only way to have life is to keep the commandments as the apple of your eye, and that includes the command not to eat garbage and not to overeat. The Most High wants a fit army. You cannot step in the street teaching people discipline when you yourself do not have it.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:4
precepts.why:
If the law is holy and just and good, then what is it to break it? “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.”

The law of the beasts in Leviticus 11 was given “to make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.” Some animals are clean and some are unclean; it is basic. So eating the unclean, pork, lobster, shrimp, oysters, snails (escargot is just French for snails), crabs, chitlins, pig feet, is transgressing the law, and transgressing the law is sin.

Overeating is sin too. Brothers who are strong in many areas, who left the porn, the smoking and the stealing when they came to the truth, still cannot say, I am not going to overeat any more. There is one area kicking their butt, to the point where they will lie about it: drinking from the brother’s slurpee on the way back from the store, eating the whole house’s bread and saying nah with the crumbs all over the bed. Where there is one sin there are many more; a demon does not walk by itself.

So keeping the holy law means keeping all of it. Gluttony and unclean food are not small things outside the commandments; they are the transgression of the law, and that is sin.

precepts.label: Romans 6:23
precepts.why:
And what does sin pay? “For the wages of sin is death”. So eating pork is going to kill you. Overeating is going to kill you. Aren’t you supposed to be the temple of God? If you keep eating a certain way, you are destroying yourself, and God will destroy him that destroys the body.

If you do not care about the vehicle the Most High gave you, how will you do the job we are all called here to do? When it is time for missions you cannot go. Brothers over a certain weight class cannot go to camp, and many will fall out of the truth over it: first staying home, then every week a different story, sick, the sniffles, until they find out they love food more than they love the Lord. God forbid something pops off at camp and you become a liability.

As we prepare for the end, get your eating under control. They can starve you for five days, then put you in a room with a Thanksgiving dinner, and you will spill your guts, just as in the Maccabees they tried to make them eat pork. If you cannot control yourself around a slurpee, you will betray this truth for fried chicken.

The law is holy, and keeping it is life; transgressing it is sin, and the wages of sin is death. We warn you because we are trying to save your life. When the high cholesterol, the high blood pressure and the diabetes hit you, you will remember these classes.

precepts.label: Sirach 18:30-31
precepts.why:
“Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats”: food is for nourishment. “Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord”. Paul moves from food to fornication because the two are correlated: both deal with self-control over your vessel, which was created as a vessel of righteousness to be used for the master's work.

Sirach says: “Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites.” You might think it is only talking about sex, but your appetite can be anything you overindulge in: food, sex, working out, TV and entertainment, sports, scrolling. We focus on food and sex because they are one and the same, and if we get control over those two we can get control of anything in our life and reprogram our vessel to do what the Lord commands.

There are wants and there are needs. You need sex, in marriage; when you do not need, study, pray, fast. You are hungry, you eat and nourish your body, then you choose the foods that give you the energy to think, function and be productive in this work. That is what food is for.

“If thou givest thy soul the desires that please her, she will make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies that malign thee.” You become a laughingstock. There are videos saying, I can't listen to a fat prophet. A brother is powerful in the street, cutting people up, bad to the bone, and people say, I can't listen to you because you don't even listen to you. That is why they say bring back fat-shaming: you are operating outside the realm of discipline.

Satan tells you that you are hungry; Satan tells you to eat that McDonald's, that Burger King, that candy. These things are pushed on us to keep us sickly so we cannot do the work, sick every Sabbath. Feed the body the vitamins, fiber and nutrients it needs, so you possess your vessel and it serves the Lord.

precepts.label: 1 John 2:15-16
precepts.why:
“All things are lawful unto me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any.” John shows the power we must not come under: “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.”

The world here is predominantly America. America is the kingdom of sin, specifically designed and created against us, in complete opposition to us, to cater to and test the flesh. It is either to make you or break you, to forge you or destroy you. Only the strong, spiritually, mentally and physically, are going to survive this kingdom.

Do not love the things catered to us in entertainment, catered to us when we are bored and idle. Scrolling is idle; that is love of the world. Porn is love of the world. Instagram models are love of the world. Clubbing is love of the world.

“For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” Satan was given power over this world, and he is going to try to get you to operate outside of your purpose. What looks good to the eyes and caters to the appetite is not always good; look past the outside to the ingredients. The body is not for any of that; it is for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

precepts.label: Psalms 136:8-17
precepts.why:
Paul says God “will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape”. There is no temptation that should derail us from inheriting the wide place, the kingdom that sits within the narrow passage (2 Esdras 7), because God's mercies endure for ever. David shows that mercy: “The sun to rule by day: for his mercy endureth for ever: The moon and stars to rule by night: for his mercy endureth for ever.” The Lord declared the end from the beginning and created all of this. We acknowledge his greatness and his mercy, and we tap into that comfort under the shadow of his wings.

“To him that smote Egypt in their firstborn: for his mercy endureth for ever: And brought out Israel from among them”. The Most High killed our enemies for us because he had mercy on us. We cried in Egypt, the Lord heard our cries and said, go down, Moses, tell Pharaoh to let my people go, or I will kill his firstborn.

“With a strong hand, and with a stretched out arm”, “To him which divided the Red sea into parts”, “And made Israel to pass through the midst of it”, “But overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red sea”, “To him which led his people through the wilderness”, “To him which smote great kings: for his mercy endureth for ever”.

We saw all of this, and we still get here today and do evil, just as our fathers under the cloud did. The Most High is trying to set us back up, but he wants to make sure we are in the right spiritual posture to inherit the kingdom. He lets us use his Bible as spiritual weapons to fight off the evil temptations so we can get to the wide.

precepts.label: Lamentations 3:20-24
precepts.why:
Paul says the things that happened to our fathers “are written for our admonition”. Jeremiah shows how we hold on to them: “My soul hath them still in remembrance, and is humbled in me.” The them is the afflictions and punishments we are supposed to remember for breaking God's commandments in the past, and we are humbled because of it.

“This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope. It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” Do you hear that? That is the love the Lord has for us, his mercy enduring for ever. He loves you, sisters; he loves you, brothers. His compassions and his mercies fail not.

“They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” His mercies are renewed every day, forgiving us. We say the Lord's prayer, we ask the Lord for mercy and to forgive our transgressions, and he does it. And we are still playing with sin.

“The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.” So now we are in the posture where he has given us a way to escape the evil all around us.

precepts.label: Psalms 23:5
precepts.why:
God will with the temptation “make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” While we endure the encounters of temptation that are common to us all, even the temptations of our own lusts, the Lord prepares a table for us: “Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.” Why? Because his mercies endure for ever.

The table is the Bible. Habakkuk shows it: “Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables”. Isaiah shows it: “write it before them in a table, and note it in a book”. The tables are what we are supposed to be reading.

But we read the tables and talk about what's going on overseas while our own spirit is rotten. We read it like entertainment instead of changing what is really going on in us.

Brothers and sisters, you are in the greatest place on the planet earth, and some of you don't even realize it. You are getting teaching that tells you what is happening in the future, because we know the future from reading the Bible. And some of you play games, scorn what is brought out, and take this for a joke. The table is prepared in the presence of our enemies; eat from it.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 2:2
precepts.why:
The table the Lord prepares before us in the presence of our enemies is the Bible. Habakkuk shows it: “And the Lord answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

The Lord told the prophet Habakkuk: since you want to get out of captivity, write the vision down, and make it plain upon the tables. That is what we are supposed to be reading.

Make it plain “that he may run that readeth it”: when we bring this out, everybody is going to be running, and we are going to run to teach it. The Bible is going to turn this whole system upside down: these are they which have turned the world upside down. But we have to be in it like that, not reading about overseas like entertainment while our own spirit is rotten.

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:8
precepts.why:
Paul says what happened to our fathers is “written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.” Isaiah shows why it was written: “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever”.

This is to the wicked Israelites, us, our people. Go write it before them in a table, and put a note in the book about their wickedness, our wickedness, “that it may be for the time to come”: for today.

And it goes on: “That this is a rebellious people”. That is what is going on with our people; our people are rebellious. But the Bible is here to correct you and straighten you out. If you want it, there is a way for you to get it.

Those who refuse to learn from the past by reading it are doomed to repeat it. You will repeat it because you refuse to learn, and the same spirits will follow you and attach themselves to you, the way people move to a new town, a new job or a new congregation and the same problem follows. The Lord sends those spirits as a mirror to show you what is wrong in you. Learn it from the book, and you won't have to learn it again.
