thread.text: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Daniel 9:2-6
precepts.why:
“But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord”. This book is the glass of the glory of the Lord, and we behold it with an open face. What is the open face? Daniel shows it: “And I set my face unto the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes”. He went to God openly by prayer and supplication.

But first, “I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem.” Seeking God openly, he went to the book, the writings of Jeremiah. Then he made his confession: “We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments”.

“Neither have we hearkened unto thy servants the prophets, which spake in thy name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.” They would not listen to the servants God sent to show them what they were doing wrong.

So when we really behold his face openly, we “are changed into the same image from glory to glory”. There is supposed to be a change in us when we pray, accept and understand that we have sinned against God. We behold ourselves in these books, and what we see there is there for us to fix. The worst thing to do is deny it, or refuse to hearken to the prophets he sends to show us how to get right.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 4:1-3
precepts.why:
Beholding with open face, we are changed. Then chapter 4: “Therefore seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not; But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty”. That is what we are supposed to do when we seek him openly, face to face: renounce the hidden things, the secret sins.

“not walking in craftiness”: not talking too much, trying to find a way to snake around it, “nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.” Blessed is the man whose conscience does not condemn him, because he has examined himself against this book, renounced what he was doing, and no longer does it.

“But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost”. If you do not understand that you have to behold with an open face and renounce sin, you are lost. That is the Christian church: we are no longer under the laws of God, we are under grace, you can't call me a sinner, I've been saved. Bro, what are you talking about? You have not renounced the hidden things of dishonesty. You're an undercover homo. You're still fornicating, still smoking weed, effeminate, popping gum with your sister's lip gloss on. You have not renounced it, so you are lost.

If you think you found God while the secret life never changes, your religion is vain. It is a level of insanity to ask God to deal with you and then not do what God says. The change from glory to glory comes only when the hidden things are renounced.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 16:63
precepts.why:
Paul says we “have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty”. Why must they be renounced and not hidden? “Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.”

God knows your inventions and the thoughts of your heart. He knows them that sin and would hide their sin. You cannot openly seek his face while you are hiding your sins, trying to get around them and not deal with them.

The open face of 2 Corinthians 3:18 is a face with nothing hidden. Beholding the glory of the Lord in his book means seeing what is there about ourselves and bringing it into the light: not walking in craftiness, not snaking around it, not handling the word of God deceitfully.

So the man who hides his sin is not beholding with an open face, and he is not changed into the same image from glory to glory. He only fools himself, because the Lord already knows what he thinks in his heart.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:3-4
precepts.why:
“But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost”. Who are the lost? Ezra shows it: “I brought you up with gladness; but with sorrow and heaviness have I lost you: for ye have sinned before the Lord your God, and done that thing that is evil before him.”

The gospel is hid to them that are lost: to him that is still in sin and has not renounced the hidden things of dishonesty. Those are the ones that are lost, still in sin, refusing to stop being dishonest and living as a sinner. If you think you found God while you live like that, you are lost. Your religion is vain and you do not really believe.

“But what shall I now do unto you? I am a widow and forsaken: go your way, O my children, and ask mercy of the Lord.”

So beholding the glory of the Lord with an open face must bring a change. Christ showed Peter his errors before he was converted, telling him he would deny him thrice, and afterward Peter was the head of the church. God opens his book and shows us, and sends prophets to show us how to get right. It does not feel good, like medicine, but if you are sincere you take it and get better. If you do not, you remain lost, and you become an example of what not to do.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 4:18
thread.text: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.

classes.title: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:4
precepts.why:
“for the things which are seen are temporal”: the things we see now are temporary. They are not going to last forever, so there is no need for us to get caught up in the things of the world. The United States of America is the world superpower and influences the whole world. Whatever music is played in America, whatever is in pop culture, the whole world responds to it. But this regime, this power, will fall, thus saith the Lord. Now we have to put our focus on overcoming the beast.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life”. Anybody in this war against evil does not entangle himself with the affairs of this life, “that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” Who chose us? Our Lord and Saviour, Jesus the Christ. He chose us to be soldiers in his military.

When Ezekiel saw that exceeding great army, he saw purple and gold. Who else is out there as foot soldiers, going nation to nation, island to island, land to land, teaching the word of God? It is not to boast; it is just the reality.

So a soldier keeps his eyes on what is not seen. We do not see the kingdom right now, but the Lord lets us know it will last forever. The Lord is doing his job; it is time for us to do ours.

precepts.label: Romans 12:2
precepts.why:
“the things which are not seen are eternal” We do not see the kingdom yet, but it will last forever. So we have to stack our bricks, and we cannot be situational Israelites. We have to be in the spirit and move in the spirit, knowing our eternal home awaits us. It is a spiritual battle, a spiritual war.

“And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”. We have to change by the renewing of our minds, because we are now new creatures in Christ. The mindset has to change.

Those things that used to trip us up so often and so easily in the world, in this day and age, cannot keep doing it. If you feel Satan raising up his head against you, if you feel that old man coming back, you have to do any and everything to deaden that spirit. Now ain't the time for that.

That is what it means to look not at the things which are seen. The world presses its pop culture and pleasures on us, but a mind renewed stays fixed on the eternal kingdom rather than conforming to a power that is about to fall.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:1
precepts.why:
“Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight”: everything that is trying to keep us from serving our God. That is exactly what sin does. “For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” The earthly tabernacle is our flesh. We were born and shapen in iniquity, so understand the condition of the battle: we will fight against our flesh until we die or until Christ returns.

A lot of people think that when they come into the truth, things will just go away. Some things you stop doing: eating pork, breaking the Lord's Sabbath, not wearing fringes, shaving your beard. You start keeping the commandments, your reasonable service. But hatred, lust and covetousness do not go away. You learn how to cope with them, and you have to prove yourself to the Lord that you are able to keep that Negro in check, that Latino in check.

“and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us”. We do not have a lot of time left. Now is high time to wake up out of sleep and fight this battle right here. We are not worried about the war in Iran; God already has that. We need to worry about the war on the day-to-day.

That is looking at the things which are not seen: running the race with patience toward the eternal, not weighed down by the temporal.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 7:31
precepts.why:
This kingdom will go down. It will pass away just like everything else. “And they that use this world, as not abusing it: for the fashion of this world passeth away.” You can use the things of this world, but do not get caught up. Do not hit the snooze button, do not abuse it, and do not lean on the things of this world over Christ.

If we really believe this Bible, we know the things of this world are going to pass away, and that fear should kick in on its own. Someone should not always have to check you. You read the Bible just like the next man. We understand young spirits, but eventually, as you walk, you check yourself.

You should become skilful in the word of God. “Wisdom raineth down skill and knowledge of understanding standing, and exalteth them to honour that hold her fast.” If wisdom is walking with you, if Christ is in you, by default you become skilful in the word and in how to apply wisdom in certain situations. You embody Christ, and everybody can see wisdom walking with you.

So the things seen are temporal and the fashion of this world passes away, while the things not seen are eternal. Use the world lightly and hold fast to wisdom.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 10:4-6
thread.text: (For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds;)

classes.title: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.label: Psalms 85:11
precepts.why:
“For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. You are at war right now in your spirit, with evil temptations pushed on every front: family members, school, work, even your own thoughts as you sit here. The weapons are not guns; the weapons are the commandments of God, and they are mighty.

Mighty to pull down what? Lies. That is what the Bible does; that is how we tear the lies down. We open up the Bible and swallow up the lies, like it says in the Psalms: “Truth shall spring out of the earth; and righteousness shall look down from heaven.” We open this Bible, and the lies are swallowed up.

So “Casting down imaginations” is casting down lies, “and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God”, and the knowledge of God is the law, the Bible. When you open this Bible and apply the commandments, you get rid of those impulsive, sinful thoughts and bring every thought “into captivity” under the obedience of Christ. That is how you walk straight past your temptation.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 8:11
precepts.why:
The weapons of our warfare are the commandments. You are supposed to answer your impulses, your sinful temptations, with the commandments of God, and that is supposed to turn you from the door of temptation. If you understood that death is around the corner, you would listen to these laws.

But the wicked man thinks judgment is far off: “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.” Because the judgment is not immediate, his sick, evil mind is emboldened to commit evil and sin, and he leaves the commandments to the side. You had better recognize where you are.

That is the war inside you. The Lord isn't asking you to pick up a gun and go do something out there; he is asking you to get your mind right and set this mark in your head to change your behavior. We don't advocate anyone initiating aggression; if someone comes at you with a rope or a knife, you defend yourself. But the gung-ho brothers who can't wait for war can't even discipline their food. The war to win first is against the heart that sin makes bold.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 14:13
precepts.why:
“And having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.” Some of our people can't wait: they want to be part of the war in the streets, casting out demons, getting their names on the Saturday night specials: brother, get a good angle of me, I want my video to go up Saturday. But here's the stipulation: when your obedience is fulfilled. That means there is no impediment left in your spirit to commit sin; you are walking straight in your spirit, your household, with your children, blameless. Then you can go out and correct your people.

That is what the Apocrypha says: “Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people”. First set your house in order. Your physical house can't be set in order if your spiritual house, meaning your damn head, is not in order. You haven't even checked your own wicked thoughts, your own actions, your own temptations, and you are trying to correct your wife, your son and your daughter.

Set your head in order; then you can set your house in order; then you can reprove your people. That is when your obedience is fulfilled, and you can revenge all disobedience, because you checked it first within yourself. precepts.label: Romans 13:14
precepts.why:
“Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” What does it mean to walk in the Spirit? It does not mean moonwalking or walking on the air. Romans explains it: “But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ”, that is, the commandments and your faith, “and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.” To make provision for the flesh is not walking in the Spirit.

To make provision is to make a way for you to fulfil that lust, leaving doors open for the sin. Why are you on the phone with your ex? You are going to end up banging her. If you are struggling, delete Instagram and delete certain things; put controls on your phone so you cannot go on certain things. People say, I made a mistake, I slipped and fell, I don't know what happened. So you were walking and just slipped and fell on the dude? There was planning. You were talking to him first, and you planned what day to meet up. It was already in your mind. It was a decision, not a mistake.

With porn, if it is that bad, get rid of social media. Do not say, I can handle it, I'm good. That is Satan telling you that, and leaving it open keeps fuelling the lust, because every time you go on you see a bunch of different stuff. Some of you say you repented but leave little doors open, and you fall back into that sin. Sit down and talk to yourself: I am dealing with this, so I need to set things up so I do not fall into it.

Because “the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”. It is a war: you want to stop, you stop for a week or two, and it comes back. The works of the flesh are “Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness”, all sexual sins. That discipline applies in marriage too: forty or eighty days after your wife gives birth, and her seven days. Satan does not come when you are dealing with your woman; he comes when you are not getting any. Those are the days to fast more and occupy yourself with the Lord. As men we cannot let pleasure control us.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 1:5
precepts.why:
Paul speaks of those “Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.” When we overindulge excessively, outside the guidelines God gave us, we start to operate outside the realm of God, outside the realm of discipline, and into the realm of Satan. That is why God gave us a law.

“For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding.” The Bible says discipline is a holy spirit. There is a cap and a limit. The man who cannot stop eating is worshipping himself, because God says to eat in moderation and to eat what nourishes; do not eat just to eat. Christ said his meat was to do the will of the Father, but people followed him just for the food, because their god was the belly.

Discipline has to be practiced. People wonder why they cannot obtain discipline: it is because they do not have the Holy Spirit. There is a level of the Holy Spirit given to you because you know your nationality, but there are levels to accessing it and gaining power in it. The disciples reached the level where they worked miracles.

Full access to the Holy Spirit comes through disciplining our food intake and our sex outtake. Food and sex are closely related in the body: one is for procreation of life, the other for nourishing that life. Those two are our stumbling blocks, the two things that keep us from progressing and moving forward.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:29
precepts.why:
“Be not excessive toward any; and without discretion do nothing.” Do not be excessive toward anything. You might say, but I am hungry. Then ask yourself why you are eating. Is it for nourishment, the proper nutrients? Or because it looks good, smells good, tastes good, because you like the sound of it? Are outside things programming you, catering to the lust of the flesh through your eyes and your ears? Did you eat just five minutes ago and now you have to get a snack?

Some are excessive even with sex, a nymphomaniac, wanting sex all the time. Sex was created for procreation; outside of that it becomes pleasure. How much pleasure until the body is completely fulfilled? There is never an end to it. The same with weed: what high are you looking for, when you always come down? There is no fulfillment in smoking weed, drinking alcohol, the excess of sex, or overeating.

That is why the scriptures speak of the holy spirit of discipline. The only fulfillment is in disciplining your spirit and keeping God’s commandments. Once you go outside the realm of discipline, you are catering to the realm of Satan, and you open yourself to be a target and to be controlled at any level. That is the mind of those who “mind earthly things” in Philippians 3.

precepts.label: Romans 16:18
precepts.why:
“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly.” This is the same people Paul wept over in Philippians 3, “whose God is their belly”: the wicked of our people. The scribes and Pharisees could not resist the wisdom of Christ or deny his miracles, but they loved the position Rome placed them in, the accolades, the greetings in the marketplace, and what comes with authority: food and sex. They crept into women’s houses as in Susanna; Eli’s sons exploited the women at the temple, because position and status bring money, power and respect.

They serve their own fleshly pleasures and lusts: let me get over on this person, let me defraud him, let me steal, so I can fill my own belly. Biggie said he was only selling crack to feed his family. He did not serve the Lord Jesus Christ; his own stomach became his god.

Your vessel is an indicator of who you serve. By the way you look, carry yourself, your conduct, your speech and your character, we can tell who your master is. People are going to get mad, but if you are grotesquely overweight, outside the realm of a natural diet, then you are your own god. You say you do not celebrate birthdays, the highest satanic celebration of oneself, yet if you cannot control your food intake, your god is your belly, and that is you.

The good thing is you can control it and do something about it, just like you control whether you celebrate birthdays. God looks at things differently than we do, so we have to reframe our mindset into the mind of Christ and the Father.

precepts.label: Psalms 119:142
precepts.why:
Christians take this chapter and say every creature is good to eat, so long as you pray over it. But Paul says the meats God created are “to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.” So what is the truth? “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The truth is the law.

That changes the whole verse. The meat is not received by everybody who bows his head over his plate. It is received by them that know the law. People say, just give thanks, just pray on it, and it's all right. Then can I pray on a human's foot and eat it? Pork carries the worm that lives in the muscle and can go to your brain; the shrimp, the lobster, the catfish and all the shellfish are bottom feeders whose job is to clean the ocean, the roaches of the sea. A prayer does not change what they are.

“For every creature of God is good” means what Genesis means: “God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good to serve its purpose. Worms prepare the land for planting, but we don't eat worms. The pig was the garbage disposal before there were trucks to pick up the garbage. Good for its work, not for your plate.

And Paul finishes: “For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” A Christian never reads up to that verse. The word of God is the law, the truth, and the law is what tells you which creatures are sanctified to eat. Many who have come into the truth, who know Christ is black and that we are Israel, are still struggling with that pork and that shrimp. This is the answer to that struggle: the ones who receive it with thanksgiving are those who know the law.

precepts.label: Sirach 32:24
precepts.why:
Paul says the meats are received “of them which believe and know the truth.” What is it to believe? “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment”. If you take heed to the commandments, you believe. Does a Christian believe in the commandments? So when he says you can eat anything as long as you receive it with thanksgiving, no: you can pray all you want, but you don't believe and you don't know the truth. Those are the very things that can save your life.

Finish the verse: “and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” If you believe in the commandments and keep the dietary laws, will you be worrying about high blood pressure? Will you be worrying about a foot amputation because of diabetes, about high cholesterol, about gout that takes brothers' fingers and feet? No, because you are not eating in a way where those sicknesses can come your way. The law tells you the food you can eat and the food you cannot eat.

All of that comes because people wanted to eat nasty, dirty food the Lord said don't eat. So take heed to yourself. Believing is not a prayer said over the plate; it is taking heed to the commandment, and the one who does fares never the worse.

precepts.label: Leviticus 11:46
precepts.why:
Paul says the meat “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” So where were the animals sanctified to be eaten or not to be eaten? In the law.

Leviticus 11 closes: “For I am the Lord your God: ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He repeats it: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” How do you become holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. To sanctify yourself and be holy you have to apply the law, the statutes and the commandments.

Then: “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.” This law takes in all the animals, whether they live on the earth or in the waters. That is how the word sanctifies the meat: by making a difference between what can be eaten and what cannot. Some animals are clean, some are unclean. It is basic.

The churches don't want you to learn the Old Testament, because they don't want you to be saved. “Keep my commandments, and live”. If you don't keep the law you are not going to live. John says “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food is sin; eating pork is going to kill you, and overeating is going to kill you.

You are supposed to be the temple of God. If you keep destroying yourself with the way you eat, you are working against what the Lord says, and against the work we are all called here to do. The meat that is received with thanksgiving is the meat the law sanctified.

precepts.label: Psalms 42:5
precepts.why:
“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear”. When fear or trouble tries to put you down, David shows how to talk to your own soul: “Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance.”

David is speaking to himself, to his soul. Put plain: I might be down, but I'm not broken. I might be down, but I'm not out yet. Satan tried to take me out, but I'm still fighting. My hope is in the Lord, and I still have some fight in me.

Some of you are quick to give up. As soon as something happens, you run out: why did they have to put correction? Correction is a good thing. It keeps you on your toes, it makes you better and stronger. What doesn't break you makes you stronger; that is correction, that is the word of God. You can use a brother's correction to build yourself up: in my mind I was going to do what this brother got corrected for, so let me move from it. Moses said some you correct openly, so that others fear. Some of you never were corrected in your life until you came to IUIC, and you are too prideful to take it.

Brothers, never keep a yes-man around you. If you have a man in your circle who cannot say, bro, I don't think you should do this, that man hates you and is waiting for your downfall. You want men who tell you, don't talk evil of leadership; if you have a problem with a brother, go to him. Sisters are the same: the sister who won't tell you what you want to hear is not your enemy, she is the one you want around you, because she has no respect of persons. Men like that help you get the kingdom of heaven.

precepts.label: Psalms 38:8-9
precepts.why:
David was down but not out, and he did not hide it from God: “I am feeble and sore broken: I have roared by reason of the disquietness of my heart.” To roar is to utter or express in a loud tone: to cry, shout, yell. David says, I'm feeble, I'm broken, and I cried out because of the disquietness of my heart.

“Lord, all my desire is before thee; and my groaning is not hid from thee.” He laid it all before the Lord.

Some of you, when you pray, do not pray for yourself, because you think you are perfect. You need to pray for yourself and ask for help to overcome certain things. Some of you are fighting lust; when you fast, pray that Messiah helps you overcome that lust. We all have lust. Our lust might be different things, but we all have it. Some of you are fighting a covetous spirit; pray that Messiah helps you overcome it.

You are not going to walk into the kingdom of heaven thinking you're perfect and your stuff don't stink. Put your desire and your groaning before the Lord, so that when the storm comes, fear does not overtake you.

precepts.label: Revelation 2:26
precepts.why:
You won't walk into the kingdom thinking you are perfect. This is what Christ said: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations”.

The word is overcome. Brothers, you must overcome the lust of America, and you must also overcome the personal thing you struggle with. We all struggle with things. Some of you struggle with lust, with porn, with prostitution, with drugs. Some of you are crackheads, weed heads; some of you it's cigarettes, Black and Milds, women. And yes, it is said to shame you. This is not my word; don't get mad at me. Read what Christ says you have to do.

The words “keepeth my works” mean keep my commandments, keep my laws. My works is this book: keep it. If you keep it, that means you have overcome. You must overcome, or else you are not going to make it to the kingdom.

So when you watch all these prophecies happen, don't include yourself if you won't let the lust go. Some of you need to let things go. That is how you keep from the spirit of fear: you prepare your mind in the scriptures and overcome, so that Esau has nothing to hold over you and you don't betray your brother to hide what you were watching.

precepts.label: Sirach 2:5
precepts.why:
“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” You are that gold. We are that gold. How do you purify gold? By putting it in the fire. Some of you need to go into the fire. You have stuff on you that has to be purged out, but you want to keep it and still have the kingdom of heaven. If you don't want to be purged, you cannot get the kingdom. Some of you want to be iron, some of you want to be silver; you have to be that gold.

What is the purpose of going through all that and not getting the kingdom? Esau has been putting you through hell all your life, and you end up missing the kingdom because you hold on to things and don't want God to take the unclean out of you.

Some of you hold on to things that happened fifty years ago, twenty years ago, five years ago. That's like a woman in an argument: you're talking about the orange and she says, yeah, but the pineapple happened five years ago. There's no pineapple here; we're talking about the orange. Some sisters got notes, waiting to bring them out. Men should not be emotional like that.

And “acceptable men in the furnace of adversity”: it takes a strong man to take correction. Weak men cannot. When correction comes, the strong man gets up, repents and keeps moving, and you can tell he is still in the fight. When you get correction, that's when you push harder. Don't lay back. Prove to Messiah, not to leadership, that you are still in the fight.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 51:12-21
precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God.” How do we ask of God? Do you think wisdom just floats down from heaven? No. You have to study; you have to open the book. And how do you know unless you have a teacher? Somebody has to teach you. As you grow in understanding you realize, like Paul, an expert in the law, that you had not known sin but by the law: I didn't know this was covetousness. Now you know what you have to fix in you.

Ecclesiasticus shows the man who asked: “When I was yet young, or ever I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer. I prayed for her before the temple, and will seek her out even to the end.” He seeks wisdom to the end because wisdom will direct your path. “For thou savedst me from destruction, and deliveredst me from the evil time: therefore will I give thanks, and praise thee”: I will thank you because you will deliver me from that evil path.

“I directed my soul unto her, and I found her in pureness.” I redirected what I was doing and directed my soul to wisdom, because wisdom in its pureness will direct my path and save me. You want to be tethered to wisdom because with wisdom you avoid the punishment. That's what we all want: to get ourselves right, to be a better servant, a better husband, a better father. Teach me, God. Well, somebody has to teach you.

“I have had my heart joined with her from the beginning, therefore shall I not be forsaken. My heart was troubled in seeking her: therefore have I gotten a good possession.” As you seek her, you start realizing all the issues you have, and the severity of what God is talking about: eternal damnation, some learning it after death by pain. I can't get past this porn, I can't get past lying. At first it sounds good: I put on fringes, we keep the feast days, we turn up. But now I'm learning, damn, I'm a hateful ass brother, I'm a murmurer, I'm a backbiter. My heart is troubled.

Then: “Draw near unto me, ye unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.” You come to the house of learning, and somebody is going to teach you how to direct yourself. So now they're teaching you, and now you're mad? Do we understand what we signed up for? You said you wanted wisdom; here it is. No, you don't really want wisdom. You want church.

precepts.label: Psalms 139:23-24
precepts.why:
If any man lack wisdom, let him ask of God: you pray, you ask of God, then you go to a house of learning and you learn. And what are you asking for? “Search me, O God, and know my heart”: know what I think, how I process your information. “try me, and know my thoughts”: I'm asking God to measure me against his word.

“And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.” Tell me, Lord, if there's any wicked way in me, and lead me in the right way. That's what we are all asking God to do: show us. So when you ask God for wisdom and he starts showing you your errors, that is the prayer being answered.

That's why James says, “My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations.” You count it joy because you asked, show me all my wicked ways so I can fix them. “But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” You ask God to show you, the scripture comes correcting you, and now you're wavering. What are you doing when you waver? Trying to dodge correction.

So when it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. It's not the sin a person commits so much as what they do afterwards that shows who they are, because none of us is right. Do they take their medicine, the scriptures? Big talk, and as soon as correction comes, they ghost and make excuses. Blessed is the man that endures it: just listen, learn, and live.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 4:26
precepts.why:
“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” You ask God in faith to show you about you so you can fix you, knowing he will direct you on the right path. “For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” Now you have asked God to show you, the scripture comes to you correcting, and you are wavering. What are you trying to do when you waver? You are trying to dodge correction.

Sirach says it: “Be not ashamed to confess thy sins; and force not the course of the river.” Here is the river, flowing. You are trying to reroute it away from you, trying to make it go another direction. You are dodging correction and making it seem like something it is not.

That is the double minded man, “unstable in all his ways”: always tossed around, forever moving, never straight, never steady, never going head on. With God “is no variableness”; with man there is variableness: jumping all over the place, can’t take it, making excuses, always responding, always having something to say, never listening. Some start answering before you can even finish the sentence; they are not listening to understand, they are listening to respond. A man of wisdom listens from a neutral position, takes in all the information, then discerns whether it fits him.

You said you wanted wisdom. Here it is. So don’t be ashamed to confess your sins, and don’t force the course of the river.

precepts.label: Amos 5:24
precepts.why:
The one who wavers is trying to dodge correction, to force the course of the river. Amos shows the river as it should flow: “But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.”

That is a river. Let judgment run down as waters. Let it run. Don’t waver and try to get around it; don’t try to force the course to divert it. Let judgment come down, and righteousness as a mighty stream.

You asked God to show you your errors, and he is showing you. “For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed. For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.” If you keep rerouting the judgment away from yourself, you will not receive the wisdom you asked for. Let it run down on you, accept it, and fix what it shows you.

precepts.label: Micah 7:9
precepts.why:
“I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him.” What is that person saying? He is taking accountability: I will bear the judgment of God, because I have sinned. “until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.”

Don’t try to get around the cause. Don’t try to deviate from the judgment. Don’t make excuses. Stop wavering. You asked God to show you, he has shown you where you are wrong, and now you are trying to bypass it: maybe I would be better if you brothers called me and checked in on me; it’s your fault. Do you think this is Disney and this is a ride? You can ride that pony by yourself.

Why will he bring me forth to the light? Because I don’t dodge what I asked for. I asked God to show me my secret faults and my errors because I want to get better, and now that he is showing me, this is not the time to start dodging. We all fall short.

How do you endure in the truth? Listen, learn and live. There is no special recipe: when it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. As soon as the medicine comes, people start running. The infraction does not tell who a person is so much as what they do afterwards: do they take their medicine, the scriptures? If they can’t, they lose respect. All the big words mean nothing if, as soon as correction comes, they ghost and make excuses because of pride and ego.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:1
precepts.why:
When people come into this faith, the challenge is dealing with the spiritual man as opposed to the carnal man. They pray for wisdom, for discernment, to grow in the truth, and then they will not listen to the men appointed before them, because the carnal man or carnal woman does not see things spiritually. Ezra shows the spirit behind it: “Thus saith the Lord, I brought this people out of bondage, and I gave them my commandments by menservants the prophets; whom they would not hear, but despised my counsels.”

God gave his commandments by the prophets to teach the people, and they would not hear the prophets. But whose counsels did they despise? “my counsels”: God’s. The prophets open the scriptures and show you thus saith the Lord to help you overcome what you are dealing with, and when you resist, it is the counsel God truly gave you that you despise. It came through men, but God inspired it.

So whoever brings correction your way, men or women, it is for your benefit, and they are being inspired by the Lord to direct you according to the path you should walk. Be humble, be quiet and listen. They are coming out of the scriptures and showing your error. Learn; this is how we grow. The carnal man will cause you to resist the direction God wants you to grow in, and that is the wavering, double minded man who shall not receive any thing of the Lord.

All scripture is given by inspiration of God for reproof, correction and instruction in righteousness. It is not a book to tote your ego so you feel good. If the Lord showed us who we are, we would be ashamed; it is only the mercy of Christ and his promise that we are here. For us to change, somebody has to tell us what we were doing wrong, and when they do, don’t get mad.

thread.label: James 1:12-15
thread.text: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.

precepts.label: James 4:7-8
precepts.why:
“Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God.” You want to blame somebody: Lord, it ain’t me, you put that big booty woman in front of me. The Lord says stop, bro. I put the nine millimeter in front of you, but you didn’t shoot yourself; I put the knife in your hand; I put the crack pipe in the room, but you didn’t smoke it. “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Enticed is when something appeals to you and you give in; you entertain it. That is on you; that is your choice. God is just showing you what your vice is, and now that is what you are fighting.

When you are tempted, you are supposed to resist. James tells how: “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” Submit yourself to God: take the counsel. How do you resist the devil? By first submitting yourself to God.

“Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you.” How are you going to draw nigh to God? Somebody is going to teach you and you are going to learn; you go to the house of learning. That is what you are doing now. And God will draw nigh to you and give you a way to escape. “Blessed is the man that endureth temptation.” How do you know what you can endure unless you go through it? You don’t know you can bench 315 until it is on the rack. You are asking for muscles; you have to lift.

“Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” We just read that in chapter one: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” Now that you hear the correction about how to get right with God, you have excuses. You see the sin in front of you and turn away, like seeing a booger in your nose in the mirror and turning your head; the booger is still there. “receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls. But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only.” The glass is the Bible; you see yourself in it and walk away and forget. You can close the book; you are still a sinner. Submit, resist, draw nigh, and cleanse your hands.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:28
precepts.why:
“Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin.” Where is lust conceived? In your mind; that is where the root begins. Christ shows exactly how: “But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” That is how lust is conceived.

We are living in an evil world, and we all see beautiful women. A picture of an immodestly dressed woman was put on the screen and the brothers were asked one by one what they saw. One liked the way she dressed. Another said she is beautiful, but the way she dresses you have to hate that thing, she has to be modest. Another said, I have been in the world a lot longer than in the truth, so I am working on hating it. What you see on the screen you see every damn day when you go outside, and some of you break your neck walking down the street.

You have to train yourself to hate evil. It doesn’t come naturally; you cannot come to the truth and all of a sudden hate what you see out there. When you see her, train your mind: she has AIDS, she stinks, she has to be a man. If you don’t, you will always be watching and desiring these things. Older brothers with experience have matured past it; the young brothers dealing with youthful lusts have to train. Sisters, before the truth many of you walked around in miniskirts and spandex, giggling and giving out your number to every dude on the block, and now you have changed how you dress. When Christ returns there will be a modesty law set up.

So you see it, and in your mind you say, damn, I don’t mind sleeping with that. When you allow that thought, lust is conceived, and sin comes forth. But if the thought comes and you shake it off, what’s wrong with you, God is going to kill you, stop thinking like that, it is not conceived. If you sit down and entertain it, it brings forth sin. That is why Christ says adultery doesn’t start when you literally lie down with a woman; it starts in your mind. “and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” Some say I fornicated and I didn’t die; that death is damnation, your soul being destroyed. God will judge you.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 32:26
precepts.why:
“Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” We were formed in his image, in his likeness, to be righteous. The literal firstfruits given to God had to be perfect; an animal could not be spotted. And James says pure religion is “to keep himself unspotted from the world.” But we all fall short.

So who is James writing to? “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. Moses said it: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. The Most High scattered us and made our remembrance cease. That goes with Deuteronomy 28:64, where we are scattered and serve gods of wood and stone. When we were serving gods of wood and stone, we were spotted.

So James is writing to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, ones that were living as sinners. Count it joy when God starts showing you who you are. To live an unspotted life, we have to learn what we were doing wrong so we can fix it. So why are you mad? That is the whole purpose. God sends teachers to show us how to get right; we get cleansed because we are swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.

And once we are unspotted, we go out and help others the same way: to visit “the fatherless and widows in their affliction”, the ones with no guide, no hedge, nobody to lead them, so they can become unspotted too. The scattered, forgotten tribes are the firstfruits God begat with the word of truth, and the good and perfect gift from above is the wisdom that makes us clean again.

precepts.label: Hebrews 11:1
precepts.why:
“What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?” Can words save him? Because that is basically all you are giving. Some people don’t even understand what faith really is, because faith alone is just saying I believe in something. Paul defines it: “Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.”

So don’t tell me you have faith. Faith is the substance, and substance is what you can touch, what you can see, something materialized. You can have faith in your head all day long, underneath your skull; I can’t see it. The only way I will know what is in your mind is when I see action as a result of your thinking. As a man thinks, you are supposed to see the fruit of it.

Even if he or she has not achieved it yet, you can tell where they are going by how they carry themselves. On a college campus you see a student walking into the engineering building with his T-squares and architect tubes. He doesn’t have the degree yet, he is not an architect or engineer yet, but the works of his mind tell you where he is going. That is how faith is validated by action. Where there is no vision, the people perish; your mind has to manipulate the elements around you to form what you have in your head.

That is what the Lord did. The earth was without form and void, meaning it did not exist yet, but he still called it earth, because earth existed in God’s mind. Then the Spirit moved upon the face of the waters, the elements, and caused them to form the earth and the light. And he saw that the light was good: he compared what was formed to what he imagined and it agreed with the thought in his mind. Sisters do the same at the mirror; you don’t walk away until what you did with your hands matches the image in your mind, and then you say it is good. That is the power we have, but our elders were cut off from giving us basic understanding like that, and we fell asleep for centuries.

That is why the elders must set up organizational foundations, literal buildings where people can see the works of the teaching. A brother or sister naked and destitute of daily food told “Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled”, but given nothing, is still hungry. That is church, that is Christianity. “Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.”

thread.text: From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?

precepts.label: James 3:15-16
precepts.why:
James 4:1 asks, “From whence come wars and fightings among you?” When you are told something you are doing wrong and something in you is adverse to correction, right is coming in and wrong is warring against it. Captains who have sat in counsel know the look: you tell somebody they don't listen, and they squint like they are confused and repeat back what you just said. It ain't their sight that went bad. It is the battle in the mind, manifesting in the face.

James shows where that confusion comes from: “For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” The word of God is pure; there is no variableness in it, and there should be no confusion in what is being said. If you were sincere, you would say, show me the lie, help me understand, maybe I am in error. Instead you are confused, because you are warring with what is right and don't want to accept it. You have strife in your heart.

“This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.” It is deceiving you, the same deceiving we read in chapter one.

Then you wonder why good things are withheld from you and why you can't move forward. You are a liar, a thief, a murderer, an adulterer, it is being identified to you, and you cannot reason with yourself. You are struggling with yourself, and that is the war in your members.

precepts.label: James 4:10-11
precepts.why:
When a brother starts to correct you and you don't like it, what do brothers start doing? They get mad, they pull away, they hold a grudge, and then they start speaking evil of the ones who corrected them. James says: “Speak not evil one of another, brethren.”

What are you supposed to do instead? “Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord.” You are supposed to humble yourself in the sight of the Lord, because you know to do good, but you don't want to do it.

That is the war and the fighting of James 4:1, coming out of the lusts that war in your members. The correction comes in, the wrong inside wars against it, and instead of humbling yourself, the war turns outward into speaking evil of your brother. The one who humbles himself stops the war where it starts.

precepts.label: James 4:17
precepts.why:
“Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.” You know that what is being said is right, but you don't want to do it, because you are struggling. What is sin for you? Your sin is what you are struggling with. That is where the war is: you don't want to accept the prophet telling you.

That is all the people in the streets right now. You tell them what they are doing wrong and they are ready to kill you; they want to fight you for teaching the Bible. What's wrong with you? You hate to hear it because it convicts you. It is letting you know your life is in shambles, that you are evil, that you are the devil.

So the wars and fightings of James 4:1 come from knowing to do good and not doing it. The lust you are holding on to wars against the good you already know.

precepts.label: Job 9:20
precepts.why:
Part of deceiving yourself is justifying yourself. “If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me”. You are condemning yourself. The word of God, which comes from the teachers, is supposed to cleanse you, and the margin gives justify as cleanse, or clear self. So justifying yourself is deceiving yourself into thinking, I'm already cleansed, I'm already clear. Whatever the teachers have to say, the reproof and the instruction I'm receiving, I'm already clean.

When that happens, teachers, sometimes you have to let people suffer. Most people don't make the same mistake twice by accident; they choose, ignore the warnings, repeat the patterns, and expect someone else to absorb the consequences. Rescue delays the learning, and growth delayed by rescue is growth denied. David said it was good that he was afflicted. We can't carry everybody.

But teachers and instructors cannot weaponize the scriptures either, using them to correct everybody else and never our own lives. Then you are the brother that is wise and teacheth many, yet is unprofitable to himself, holding brothers to a higher accountability than you are willing to hold yourself, expecting perfection while you have hidden sins. The justified self is the one the mouth condemns, whether it is the one being corrected or the one correcting.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 9:27
precepts.why:
Peter says to “abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”, and the two biggest fleshly lusts in the world, going back to Genesis, are food and sex: one deals with nourishing and one with procreation. Paul shows how to fight that war: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.” The whole purpose is to bring our body into subjection, in what we take in through our mouth and what we take in through our eyes.

One way to keep your body in subjection: you can control your sexual appetite and your lust by controlling your food intake. The foods you desire, the foods you like, the foods you are tempted with, practice abstaining from them. Take alcohol. The brain stores alcohol with a time and an environment: late at night, social gatherings, partying, celebrating. So brothers that watch porn, try not drinking when everybody around you is drinking. If you can abstain from that, you can abstain from anything else. You are telling your flesh and your reward vectors, even though my brain says drink in this environment, I am going against what my body wants.

Or the candy you love: abstain from it. If you can abstain from the things you love, you gain control and power over the things that have even more control and power over you. You are training your body and your mind and disassociating things from it until you have full control over your vessel.

Then when it comes to sexual temptation, you tell your body, no, I am not associating this feeling with pornography, this feeling with Instagram, this feeling with looking. Disconnect that association, rewire the neurons, and fire them into a different, positive behavior. When you go into that environment, open up a Bible, do something else, and train your brain to associate that feeling with the new habit. There is a way to get complete control over it, so that having preached to others, you yourself are not a castaway.

precepts.label: Job 1:10-12
precepts.why:
Peter warns, “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. Job shows how that adversary works. Satan says to God, “Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” God had a hedge of protection around Job, and Satan wanted it taken down: “put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.”

God answers, “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” Notice what Satan was given. He could take Job's possessions and stir up his life, but he could not touch Job himself, meaning he could not control Job's actions. The devil does not make anybody do anything. He sets the stage, creates an environment to nourish his goal, and watches; you pull your own strings.

Keep reading into Job 2. Satan “smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown”, and Job sat down among the ashes. Then his wife said, “Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” Satan did not take control of her mouth. He could not get to Job, so he put the thought in the wife, the weaker vessel, because women give in to their emotions and their own thought process more than men do. She had a decision to make, and she chose to act on the thought Satan put in her.

That is the lesson for us. There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through our minds. You cannot stop a thought from coming, but agreeing with it and acting on it is your choice. America is Satan's stage; everyone acts in the play, but you choose which script you follow.

precepts.label: John 13:2
precepts.why:
“And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him”. Look at what it says the devil did: he put it into the heart of Judas. He did not reach in and move Judas's hands. He put the thought there, and Judas acted on that thought and betrayed Christ.

This is the same pattern as Job's wife. Satan works through the thought process. He watches, he looks for the one who will receive the thought, and he plants it. Everything after that is the person's own decision. That is why nobody can say, the devil made me do it. You made you do it.

Peter's warning fits right here: the adversary walks about “seeking whom he may devour”. He is searching for a heart that will take the thought and carry it out, the way Judas did.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:22-23
precepts.why:
Christ told his disciples what was coming: he would be betrayed and killed by the Pharisees, the scribes and the Sadducees. Then “Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee.” Peter was saying, I am not going to allow that to happen.

“But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.” Christ was supposed to die for the sins of the nation, and Satan whispered to Peter to stand in the way. Christ spotted Satan from a distance, and Peter did not even know Satan was there. That is how crafty and cunning Satan is.

Did Peter have good intentions? He did. But even when good is present, evil is always there. So good intentions are not enough; you have to measure and weigh the words you are about to speak and filter them through the word of God, to see whether this is God's intention or your own desires being worked on by the voice of Satan.

If your mind is not in tune with the scriptures, he can whisper something through your thoughts and take control and manipulate you. Being sober and vigilant means checking even your good ideas against the word.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 6:16
precepts.why:
Wisdom “goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably unto them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought.” The devil walks about seeking whom he may devour, and wisdom goes about seeking those worthy of her. Wisdom has to meet you in every thought.

When a thought comes to your mind, measure it: what is the outcome of this thought? Say you get into an argument with your husband. The first thought says, say this certain word, and you can trigger him and make him feel the way you feel. Those thoughts are being fed to you: say this, say this. Wisdom filters that thought and makes sure it has godly intentions before it comes out of your mouth.

Paul wrote in 2 Corinthians 13:10 that he used his words “according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.” The power God gave us is for edification. With every thought, ask: am I exhorting this person, or could the way I am saying it destroy them? Even good intentions and exhortation can land the wrong way.

It works the other way too. Someone may say something to you that was positive when they said it, but it hits you as negative because Satan knows what you are going through and used that person's vessel. Then comes the thought: why would they say that to you? Say this back. You choose whether to respond for edification or unto destruction, whether to bring contention or to wink at ignorance. Everything is a choice.

precepts.label: Genesis 4:7
precepts.why:
God told Cain, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Demons do not simply possess someone; it is a process, and they need a series of yeses. The spirits can only communicate through your thoughts and set the stage. To take full control, you have to agree with the thought, make a contract or covenant with it, and act on it. If you say, I do not agree with that, that is not according to the scriptures, the demon cannot take control of your eyes, your ears, your mouth or your tongue.

Doing well is keeping the commandments. It is a covenant with God: I am not going to watch that, eat that, touch that, taste that. Doing not well, sin lying at the door, is a covenant with death, a covenant with Satan. Satan has commandments too, and any time you disagree with keeping God's commandment, you agree to keep Satan's.

See how the yeses add up. You agree to go past the blood alcohol limit and you let a spirit take control of your body, then wonder why you slept with that person. A thought says, I do not like that sister, you agree with it and start gossiping, and now it spreads through the whole body. You know that food is not for you, but you agree with the hunger pains, the sight of it and the smell of it, and now a gluttony spirit is on you. Every contract with a thought lets the demon tunnel through the five senses to full possession of your vessel.

The answer is in Galatians 5:16: “Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” Walk in the spirit by studying, keeping a strong unit, sitting at the doorsteps of the Bishop and the Deacons, and addicting yourself to God's word, and you will not have time to entertain the flesh. Stop feeding your mind hours of shows and music that taint your thinking. Reprogram and rewire yourself to develop godly habits, because “the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”.

Christ is the example. His disciples prayed him, “Master, eat”, and he said, “I have meat to eat that ye know not of.” He was the master of his own vessel: his sight, smell, taste, hearing and thoughts. Nobody programmed him but the Father. “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.” That should be our agenda: to consume the scriptures, to see, taste, hear and believe them. That is our meat and our life.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 28:3
precepts.why:
The beast has “upon his heads the name of blasphemy”, and “he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven”: the Most High, Christ and the angels. That is what they do: they lie against God’s people and God himself. “The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies.”

Look at the Tomahawk missile that hit the elementary school in Minab, Iran, killing 175 people, mostly children. First they blamed Iran; then they said it was a mistake from outdated targeting data; then Trump said, I don’t know about it. Don’t listen for one second to these liars.

Ezekiel 28:3 answers them: “Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee”. What was Daniel able to do? Interpret dreams. America is able to interpret your next move, because they have that kind of surveillance and technological capability. The Bible prophesied it.

So if there is no secret that can be hid from America, according to God, how did they mistakenly hit a school and think it was part of a base? It was no mistake. It shows you they are crooks and liars, the beast with a mouth speaking blasphemies. And to our people still asleep and following behind the beast, even a ranking man among us who re-enlisted in the army in the middle of Bible prophecy, knowing he will be deployed: come up out of this foolishness.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:3
precepts.why:
The beast of Revelation 13 rises out of the sea “having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns”. The seven heads are Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain. The ten horns are the ten common markets, the EU, and on the military side NATO, now over thirty nations.

Revelation 12:3 shows the same creature: “And there appeared another wonder in heaven; and behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.” This heaven is rulership: who would be leading the earth, the world superpower, in the latter days. So the beast is also the red dragon, and red is the key indicator of who this is.

Genesis 25:25 tells you: “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Then “after that came his brother out”, with no description at all. Why? Because Jacob looked just like everybody else; everybody at that time had dark pigmentation. Esau was different, so he had to be described.

So the great red dragon with seven heads and ten horns is Esau, and the beast in power in the latter days is America, of the seven because the Americans came over here from Great Britain, with the ten horns giving their power and strength to it.

precepts.label: Romans 13:11
precepts.why:
The ten horns “have one mind, and shall give their power and strength unto the beast.” That is NATO, formed in 1949, with America at the front. But things are changing. France and Italy are negotiating with Iran for oil through the Strait of Hormuz; Canada says it will never take part in the offensive; Germany warns against an endless war; Spain has withdrawn its ambassador from Israel. They agreed to give their power to the beast, and now they are looking out for themselves.

So as Israelites, the blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans scattered abroad, not only here in America, when we see things like this we have to understand our salvation is getting closer. “And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed”: nearer than when we first came to the knowledge. Things are escalating rather quickly, and this conflict is something to keep our eyes on.

A lot of us do not recognize what the feast of Passover is really about: the destruction of our enemies and us being saved from their hands. How fitting that the high holy day comes in a time like this. So we have to increase our focus and buckle down; we are in the midst of war, and our minds should not be in other places.

As Deacon Yashua in Phoenix said last Sabbath: prophecy should move us to correction; it is not for our entertainment.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 2:1-2
precepts.why:
“And the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast, these shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.” Over time something will cause these kings to hate the whore, the United States of America. Trump badmouths NATO for not paying their fees and threatens to end the alliance, and now they don’t want to be drawn into a long war. They will make her desolate and naked with intercontinental ballistic missiles.

But before that comes, we have to achieve abstinence, discipline, overcoming, and unity. Zephaniah says: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”. The nation not desired is us. They call us minorities and put labels on us, blacks, Hispanics, derogatory terms wherever we are: the Dalits in India, the Afro-Iranians, the Afro-Palestinians. Wherever we are scattered we are hated and despised. But the Bible says gather together. It is all about Israelite unity, and that is what they have always feared, because if the Israelites unify, that is the end of this wicked regime.

They even lie about Amalek. Bibi Netanyahu and his crew are the Amalekites according to the Bible, so to deflect that history they call the Iranians, the Persians, present-day Amalek.

“Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you”. The decree is already made; it is prophesied, and destruction is coming. So take heed, acknowledge it, and get yourselves right.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 3:9-11
precepts.why:
Zephaniah speaks of the decree; Peter shows it will not fail: “The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness”. What the Lord said is exactly what will come to pass. He “is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.” The Lord does not want any of his people to perish, and that is why he is giving us time to get ourselves right. That does not mean he will not put the wicked to death.

“But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night”, whether you get yourself right or not, “in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. How is that possible? By nuclear fire: the same burning with fire the ten horns bring on the whore.

“Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be”? That goes to Deacon Yashua’s point. Should we sit with the popcorn just watching? Eating popcorn is not a sin, with a little butter and salt. But if that is all you are doing and you are not applying, that is when it becomes an issue.

This is not the time to kick our feet up or bug out. Now is the time to work like we never worked before and to increase in righteousness.

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:15-17
precepts.why:
“And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus”. The woman is Babylon the Great, America, and the martyrs of Jesus are the Israelites: those who stand up for this truth all the way up to the threat of death and beyond it. Many of us are going to get killed. They drank our blood by putting us in captivity and dealing evil with us.

Obadiah explains that drinking: “For the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.” The reward of what the nations did to us is coming back on them. “For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain”: what did they drink upon us? Captivity, slavery, rape, robbery, murder, lies, rigged juries, castrations, lynchings, railroading; the Rasheem Carters, the Kendrick Johnsons.

“So shall all the heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down”. All the nations that did this to God’s people will drink the captivity, the slavery, the whipped backs, the lynchings, and digest it. “And they shall be as though they had not been.” They dehumanized us until we do not even recognize we were once a great people, reduced us to nothing, when we are the jewels of God. So they will be reduced to nothing, as Isaiah 14:21 cuts off their name.

“But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions.” Deliverance is for the ones of us that repent and stop BSing. The ones who do not repent and keep up the BS, the Most High is going to wipe out along with our enemies.

precepts.label: Isaiah 13:5
precepts.why:
“The beast that thou sawest was, and is not; and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and go into perdition”. It was in John’s vision but not in his time. When it came, it came out of Europe, Great Britain to be exact. And it shall go into perdition, destruction. That is where we are now; that is what this war is signifying.

The weapons to do it are already here. You don’t have to wonder where the fire is going to come from. The Lord will come with fire because he is coming with those weapons; he is going to be literally riding on the weapons being fired, and coming with something like two hundred million angels. That is what Isaiah 13:5 says: the Lord and the weapons of his indignation come from a far country, “to destroy the whole land”, the whole land, singular.

That fire is the perdition of Babylon the Great; that is what the beast is going to get. And “they that dwell on the earth shall wonder, whose names were not written in the book of life”. They have no clue that this is Babylon the Great, and they are not getting the kingdom, no matter how many churches they set up.

Every time you pray the Lord’s prayer, thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth, you are advocating for the destruction of this kingdom. Christ is not setting his kingdom beside this one. The King of kings is coming to topple it with the weapons of his indignation.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 3:17-18
precepts.why:
In 2 Esdras 1:5 God commands the prophet: “Go thy way, and shew my people their sinful deeds”. Go and show the people. Ezekiel was given the same charge: “get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people, and speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.” Whether they hear or forbear, our job is to go and tell them.

Then God tells him why: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me. When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.”

So as a prophet and teacher, it is required that we tell you what you are doing wrong, because if we don’t, we are liable to have that blood on our hands. It is not that we even have a choice. You call yourself a prophet, a teacher: your job is to go correct the people and help the brother.

That is why showing the people their sinful deeds is not hatred. Sometimes you have to show someone their shame, and that is God loving them too, because he could leave them right there to die and find out after death. It is our job to warn our people, to hopefully bring them to repentance, and when they come, to help them reform their ways. But they have to be willing to listen, and they cannot want correction for others while refusing it for themselves.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:17
precepts.why:
If you see a brother that is in error and you don’t correct him, what does the scripture say you are? “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.”

If you see a brother in error and do not rebuke him, you hate your brother in your heart. Leaving sin upon him is not love; rebuking him in any wise is. So we have no choice but to tell our people what they are doing wrong, or we hate our brother in our heart.

That is the love behind 2 Esdras 1:5, “shew my people their sinful deeds, and their children their wickedness which they have done against me”. Showing the people their sins is how you keep from hating them. And it goes both ways: when a brother comes to you and says this is wrong, hear it and learn, because you do not want to be on the outside of what is about to happen.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 7:17-18
precepts.why:
God held Moses by him a long season and “shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”. Ezra was not the only one; God showed Solomon the same. “For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements: The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”.

God showed Solomon how the world was created, from the beginning, when he said let there be light. He showed him how the elements operate: water, air, fire. You breathe the air but do not know where it comes from; ask Solomon. There is a spirit in fire: a little fire can consume a whole place; ask Solomon how. Everything runs to the ocean, yet the ocean never overflows; ask Solomon why. Christ said you cannot even count the hairs on your head. Those things are too heavy for us, but God showed them to Solomon.

The scripture says Solomon had more knowledge than any king before him or after him, the greatest king who ever walked this planet. He knew so much that at the end the knowledge almost consumed him. And he saw the beginning, the middle and the end of time, just as Moses did.

So if a young man says, I know everything in the Bible and there is nothing anybody can teach me, you are a fool. You can spend your lifetime in this book and still not master it. Bishop Nathanyel was not teaching back then the way he teaches today; as time goes by, more of the spiritual world opens to the Bishops. We have not been shown even ten percent of what was shown to Solomon. The waters are rising; just be patient.
